params.code:
import numpy as np
import wie

c = wie.c
D_ly = 4.2465
D = D_ly * wie.ly
beta = 0.999999
v = beta * c

def gamma_of(vv):
    return 1.0 / np.sqrt(1.0 - (vv / c) ** 2)

gam = gamma_of(v)
t_earth = D / v
t_ship = t_earth / gam
L_ship = D / gam
ke_per_kg = (gam - 1.0) * c ** 2
t_light = D / c

# Hypothetical FTL signal at 10c, seen from a frame moving at 0.5c the same way
u = 10.0 * c
vo = 0.5 * c
dt_sig = D / u
dt_moving = gamma_of(vo) * (dt_sig - vo * D / c ** 2)
dt_moving_yr = dt_moving / wie.year
# speed above which any FTL signal looks backwards in time for that observer: u > c^2/vo
u_crit = c ** 2 / vo

yr = wie.year
tf = t_earth / yr
t = np.linspace(0, tf * 1.05, 220)
ts = t * yr
x_ship = np.minimum(v * ts, D) / wie.ly
x_light = np.minimum(c * ts, D) / wie.ly
x_tach = np.minimum(u * ts, D) / wie.ly
z = np.zeros_like(t)

s = wie.Scene(t, time_unit="yr", length_unit="ly")
s.body("Earth", [0, 0, 0], radius=0.08, kind="earth")
s.body("Proxima Centauri", [D_ly, 0, 0], radius=0.12, kind="star", temperature=3042)
ship_scale = np.array([1.0 / gam ** 0.25, 1.0, 1.0])
s.body("Ship at 99.9999% of c", np.c_[x_ship, z, z], radius=0.05, kind="ship", scale=ship_scale)
s.body("Light pulse", np.c_[x_light, z + 0.15, z], radius=0.03, kind="light", color="#ffffaa")
s.body("Tachyon signal (hypothetical, 10c)", np.c_[x_tach, z - 0.15, z], radius=0.03, kind="particle", color="#ff44ff")
s.curve("Route", np.array([[0, 0, 0], [D_ly, 0, 0]]), color="#5577aa", width=0.5)

ship_clock_days = np.minimum(ts, t_earth) / gam / wie.day
s.series("Ship clock", ship_clock_days, "days")
s.series("Distance covered", x_ship, "ly")

s.number("Lorentz factor at 99.9999% of c", gam, "", "time slows and distances shrink by this factor")
s.number("Trip time on Earth's clocks", t_earth / yr, "yr", "light itself takes 4.2465 yr")
s.number("Trip time on the ship's clock", t_ship / wie.day, "days", "the crew's own experience")
s.number("Kinetic energy per kg of ship", ke_per_kg, "J/kg", "(gamma - 1) c^2; infinite at exactly c")
s.number("10c signal's arrival time seen from a 0.5c frame", dt_moving_yr, "yr", "negative = arrives before it was sent")

s.caption(0, f"Relativity forbids anything with mass reaching c: the energy (gamma - 1)c^2 grows without limit. So we fly at 99.9999% of c, gamma = {gam:.1f}.")
s.caption(0.3 * tf, f"Each kilogram of ship carries {ke_per_kg:.2e} J of kinetic energy. Pushing to exactly c would need infinite energy.")
s.caption(dt_sig / yr, f"A hypothetical 10c tachyon signal arrives after {dt_sig/yr:.3f} yr. But a traveller moving at 0.5c measures it arriving {abs(dt_moving_yr):.2f} yr BEFORE it was sent: FTL means signals into the past.")
s.caption(0.7 * tf, f"Inside the ship, the {D_ly} ly trip is length-contracted to {L_ship/wie.ly*63241:.0f} AU, so the crew feels like they are moving 'faster than light'.")
s.caption(tf, f"Arrival: {t_earth/yr:.4f} yr pass on Earth, only {t_ship/wie.day:.2f} days on board. You can reach any star within your lifetime, just never beat the light pulse.")
s.caption(1.02 * tf, "Real loopholes need exotic physics: an Alcubierre warp bubble or a traversable wormhole (both need negative energy), or tachyons (never seen). ER=EPR wormholes can't carry signals.")

# checks
s.check("Ship time equals Earth time divided by gamma (independent: proper time = D sqrt(1-b^2)/v)", t_ship, D * np.sqrt(1 - beta ** 2) / v, rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Lorentz transform: 10c signal goes backwards in time because u > c^2/v", float(u > u_crit), 1.0)
s.check("Invariant interval: c^2dt^2 - dx^2 same in moving frame", (c * dt_moving) ** 2 - (gamma_of(vo) * (D - vo * dt_sig)) ** 2, (c * dt_sig) ** 2 - D ** 2, rtol=1e-9)
gps = (gamma_of(3874.0) - 1.0) * 86400 * 1e6
s.check("Baseline: GPS orbital-speed time dilation matches measured ~7.2 microseconds/day", gps, 7.2, rtol=0.02)
s.check("Baseline: Newtonian limit, kinetic energy at 30 km/s equals 0.5 v^2", (gamma_of(3e4) - 1) * c ** 2, 0.5 * 3e4 ** 2, rtol=1e-5)

s.answer(f"As far as we know you can't, because pushing anything with mass to light speed would take infinite energy. At 99.9999% of light speed (gamma = {gam:.1f}), the {D_ly} ly trip to Proxima Centauri takes {t_earth/yr:.4f} yr on Earth's clocks but only {t_ship/wie.day:.2f} days on board, so for the crew it feels faster than light. A real faster-than-light signal at 10c would be seen by an observer moving at half light speed as arriving {abs(dt_moving_yr):.2f} yr before it was sent, which means messages to the past. That is why warp drives, wormholes and tachyons all stay speculative.")
s.camera(focus="Ship at 99.9999% of c", view="top")

assumptions: Why this picture: special relativity is the consensus and forbids massive objects reaching c, so the closest possible version (99.9999% of c) is simulated.
Constant cruise speed with instant acceleration at the start and stop.
Proxima Centauri is at 4.2465 light years.

theories.name: Special relativity: light speed is a hard limit
theories.summary: Energy grows without limit as speed nears c, so massive objects can get ever closer to c but never reach it. Time dilation and length contraction still let travellers cross huge distances within their own lifetimes.

theories.name: Alcubierre warp drive
theories.summary: A bubble of flat space is carried along by contracting space in front and expanding space behind, letting the ship arrive faster than light without locally exceeding light speed. It requires large amounts of negative energy that no known matter provides.

theories.name: Traversable wormholes
theories.summary: General relativity allows tunnels joining distant regions of space, but holding one open requires exotic matter that violates the null energy condition. Known quantum setups give wormholes no faster than going the long way round.

theories.name: Tachyons
theories.summary: Hypothetical particles that always travel faster than light, with imaginary mass. They could send signals into the past, creating paradoxes, and none has ever been observed.

theories.name: ER = EPR
theories.summary: Entanglement and Einstein-Rosen bridges may be the same thing, but such bridges cannot carry signals faster than light.

spec.title: Chasing a light beam at 99.9999% of light speed
spec.question: What if you rode a beam of light?

params.code:
import numpy as np
import wie

c = wie.c
beta = 0.999999            # closest honest version: anything with mass can never reach c
v = beta * c
d = 4.2465 * wie.ly        # race a light pulse from the Sun to Proxima Centauri

def trip(dist, vel):
    g = 1.0 / np.sqrt(1.0 - (vel / c) ** 2)
    te = dist / vel
    return g, te, te / g, dist / g, (g - 1.0) * c ** 2

gamma, t_e, t_s, d_ship, ke = trip(d, v)
t_e_yr = t_e / wie.year
t_s_day = t_s / wie.day
d_ship_au = d_ship / wie.AU
lag_s = t_e - d / c                       # how far behind the light pulse you arrive
# speed of the light beam measured from the ship (relativistic velocity addition)
u_rel = (c - v) / (1.0 - v * c / c ** 2)
dopp = np.sqrt((1 + beta) / (1 - beta))
T_cmb_ahead = wie.T_cmb * dopp
theta_side = np.degrees(np.arccos(beta))
E_proton_GeV = (gamma - 1) * wie.m_p * c ** 2 / (1e9 * wie.e_charge)
E_mt = ke * 1000.0 / 4.184e15             # 1 tonne ship

F = 240
t = np.linspace(0, t_e_yr, F)
t_sec = t * wie.year
x_ship = beta * t
x_light = np.minimum(t, d / wie.ly)
s = wie.Scene(t, time_unit="years (Earth clock)", length_unit="light years")
s.body("Sun", [0, 0, 0], radius=0.12, kind="star", temperature=5772)
s.body("Proxima Centauri", [d / wie.ly, 0, 0], radius=0.08, kind="star", temperature=3042, color="#ff6a3d")
s.body("Ship", np.c_[x_ship, 0 * t, 0 * t + 0.05], radius=0.05, kind="ship", scale=[1.0 / gamma, 1.0, 1.0])
s.body("Light pulse", np.c_[x_light, 0 * t, 0 * t - 0.05], radius=0.03, kind="light", color="#fff6a0")
s.curve("Route", np.array([[0, 0, 0], [d / wie.ly, 0, 0]]), color="#66ccff", width=0.5)
s.series("Ship clock", t_sec / gamma / wie.day, "days")
s.series("Light pulse's lead over the ship", (1 - beta) * t_sec, "light seconds")

s.number("Ship speed", beta * 100, "% of light speed", "Reaching exactly 100% would need infinite energy")
s.number("Lorentz factor", gamma, "", "Your clock runs this many times slower than Earth's")
s.number("Light beam's speed measured from the ship", u_rel / 1000, "km/s", "Exactly c: you never catch up")
s.number("Trip time on the ship's clock", t_s_day, "days", f"Earth clocks: {t_e_yr:.2f} years")
s.number("Light pulse arrives ahead of you by", lag_s, "s", "Earth frame, over 4.2465 ly")
s.number("Cosmic microwave background ahead", T_cmb_ahead, "K", "Blueshifted to a glowing-hot sky")

s.caption(0, f"You race a light pulse at {beta*100:.4f}% of light speed. Exactly 100% is forbidden: the energy needed grows without limit")
s.caption(t_e_yr * 0.2, f"Yet you measure the beam beside you moving away at {u_rel/1000:.0f} km/s, the full speed of light. Einstein's frozen light wave never appears")
s.caption(t_e_yr * 0.4, f"Your Lorentz factor is {gamma:.0f}: the 4.25 ly route shrinks to {d_ship_au:.0f} AU in your frame")
s.caption(t_e_yr * 0.6, f"The sky crushes forward: stars beside you appear just {theta_side:.3f} degrees from dead ahead; the 2.7 K microwave glow ahead is now {T_cmb_ahead:.0f} K")
s.caption(t_e_yr * 0.8, f"Each interstellar proton hits you at {E_proton_GeV:.0f} GeV, LHC-class radiation")
s.caption(t_e_yr, f"Arrival: {t_e_yr:.2f} years on Earth, only {t_s_day:.2f} days on board, and the light still beat you by {lag_s:.0f} s")

s.check("Speed of light invariant: velocity addition gives c", u_rel, c, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Lorentz factor matches wie.lorentz", gamma, wie.lorentz(v), rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Spacetime interval invariant", (c * t_e) ** 2 - d ** 2, (c * t_s) ** 2, rtol=1e-6)
gs, tsun, a1, a2, a3 = trip(wie.AU, (1 - 1e-12) * c)
s.check("Baseline: near-light trip Sun to Earth equals sunlight's measured 499 s", tsun, 499.0, rtol=2e-3)
gl, tl, tsl, dl, kel = trip(d, 1e-4 * c)
s.check("Newtonian limit: KE -> v^2/2", kel, 0.5 * (1e-4 * c) ** 2, rtol=1e-6)

s.answer(f"You can never quite ride a light beam: anything with mass needs infinite energy to reach light speed, and even at {beta*100:.4f}% you still measure the beam pulling away at {u_rel/1000:.0f} km/s, so you never see light standing still. At that speed your Lorentz factor is {gamma:.0f}, so the 4.25 light year trip to Proxima Centauri takes {t_e_yr:.2f} years on Earth but only {t_s_day:.2f} days for you, and the light pulse still beats you by {lag_s:.0f} s. Ahead, the faint microwave afterglow of the Big Bang is blueshifted to {T_cmb_ahead:.0f} K and every proton you hit carries {E_proton_GeV:.0f} GeV.")
s.camera(focus="Ship", view="side")

assumptions: Riding exactly at light speed is impossible for anything with mass, so the ship flies at 99.9999% of c instead.
The ship cruises at constant speed; acceleration and braking are ignored.
The race is from the Sun to Proxima Centauri, 4.2465 light years away.
Interstellar gas is treated as a thin stream of protons; shielding is not modelled.
Flat spacetime (special relativity); the gravity of the stars is ignored.

spec.title: The Twin Paradox: A Round Trip to Proxima Centauri at 99% of Light Speed
spec.question: What if a twin travelled to a star at near light speed and came back?

params.code:
import numpy as np
import wie

c = wie.c; ly = wie.ly; yr = wie.year
d_ly = 4.2465
d = d_ly * ly
beta = 0.99
v = beta * c
age0 = 30.0

r = wie.cruise(d, v)
gam = r["gamma"]
t_e1 = r["t_earth_s"]; t_s1 = r["t_ship_s"]
T_earth = 2 * t_e1 / yr
T_ship = 2 * t_s1 / yr
gap = T_earth - T_ship
d_ship_ly = r["distance_ship_frame_m"] / ly

# Doppler bookkeeping: signals each twin sends once per year of their own time
f_out = np.sqrt((1 - beta) / (1 + beta))
f_in = np.sqrt((1 + beta) / (1 - beta))
earth_years_seen_by_ship = (t_s1 * f_out + t_s1 * f_in) / yr
t_turn_seen_on_earth = (t_e1 + d / c) / yr
rate_earth_sees_out = (t_s1 / yr) / t_turn_seen_on_earth

# realistic 1 g rocket, round trip = 2 one-way flip trips
rk = wie.rocket(d, accel=wie.g0, flip=True)
tau_rk = 2 * rk["tau_total_s"] / yr
t_rk = 2 * rk["t_total_s"] / yr
vmax_rk = rk["v_max"] / c

ke_per_kg = r["kinetic_energy_per_kg_J"]
mt_per_kg = ke_per_kg / 4.184e15

# Scene in Earth years
F = 260
t = np.linspace(0, T_earth, F)
th = t_e1 / yr
x = np.where(t <= th, beta * t, d_ly - beta * (t - th))
x = np.clip(x, 0, d_ly)
tau = t / gam
age_home = age0 + t
age_trav = age0 + tau

s = wie.Scene(t, time_unit="years (Earth clock)", length_unit="light years")
s.body("Earth", [0, 0, 0], radius=0.08, kind="earth", spin=2 * np.pi * 365.25)
s.body("Proxima Centauri", [d_ly, 0, 0], radius=0.08, kind="star", temperature=3042)
s.body("Travelling twin's ship", np.c_[x, 0 * t, 0 * t + 0.12], radius=0.05, kind="ship",
       color="#e0e8ff", scale=[1.0 / gam, 1.0, 1.0])
s.curve("Route", np.array([[0, 0, 0.12], [d_ly, 0, 0.12]]), color="#5577aa", width=0.6)

# yearly birthday light pulses sent from Earth
nP = int(np.floor(T_earth)) + 1
pts = np.full((F, nP, 3), np.nan)
for k in range(nP):
    xp = t - k
    ok = (xp >= 0) & (xp <= d_ly)
    pts[ok, k, 0] = xp[ok]
    pts[ok, k, 1] = -0.12
    pts[ok, k, 2] = 0.0
s.cloud("Earth twin's yearly birthday signals", pts, color="#ffee88", size=2.5)

s.series("Stay-at-home twin's age", age_home, "years")
s.series("Travelling twin's age", age_trav, "years")
s.series("Age gap", t - tau, "years")

s.number("Round trip on Earth's clock", T_earth, "years", "time the stay-at-home twin ages")
s.number("Round trip on the ship's clock", T_ship, "years", "time the travelling twin ages")
s.number("Age gap at reunion", gap, "years", f"at 99% of light speed, Lorentz factor {gam:.2f}")
s.number("Lorentz factor", gam, "", "how many times slower the ship's clock runs")
s.number("Realistic 1 g round trip, ship clock", tau_rk, "years", f"{t_rk:.2f} years pass on Earth, top speed {vmax_rk*100:.1f}% of c")
s.number("Kinetic energy per kg of ship", mt_per_kg, "megatons TNT", "needed for each kilogram at 99% of c")

s.caption(0, f"Both twins are {age0:.0f}. One leaves for Proxima Centauri at 99% of light speed: Lorentz factor {gam:.2f}.")
s.caption(th * 0.5, f"To the traveller the {d_ly:.4f} ly trip shrinks to {d_ship_ly:.3f} ly. Earth's birthday signals reach her stretched out, one every {1/f_out:.1f} of her years.")
s.caption(th, f"Turnaround at Proxima: {th:.2f} years have passed on Earth but only {t_s1/yr:.3f} years on board. Turning around is what breaks the symmetry.")
s.caption(th + 0.5 * (T_earth - th), f"Heading home, Earth's signals come in blueshifted {f_in:.1f} times: she watches her twin age fast, {earth_years_seen_by_ship:.2f} years of Earth birthdays in total.")
s.caption(T_earth, f"Reunion: the twin who stayed is {age0+T_earth:.2f}, the traveller is {age0+T_ship:.2f}, so she is {gap:.2f} years younger.")

s.check("Doppler count: Earth signals seen by traveller equal Earth time elapsed", earth_years_seen_by_ship, T_earth, rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Earth sees outbound ship clock at the redshifted Doppler rate", rate_earth_sees_out, f_out, rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Ship time = interval sqrt(t^2 - x^2/c^2) for each leg", t_s1, np.sqrt(t_e1**2 - (d / c)**2), rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Lorentz factor formula", gam, 1 / np.sqrt(1 - beta**2), rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Baseline: GPS satellite velocity time dilation about 7.2 microseconds per day",
        (wie.lorentz(3874.0) - 1) * 86400 * 1e6, 7.2, rtol=0.03)

s.answer(f"If one twin flies to Proxima Centauri and back at 99% of light speed, {T_earth:.2f} years pass on Earth but only {T_ship:.2f} years on the ship, so the traveller comes home {gap:.2f} years younger than her twin. This is not an illusion: her path through spacetime is shorter, and the turnaround is what makes the two twins' situations different. A more realistic rocket that accelerates and brakes at a comfortable 1 g would take {tau_rk:.2f} years of ship time while {t_rk:.2f} years pass on Earth.")
s.camera(focus="Travelling twin's ship", view="side")

assumptions: The star is Proxima Centauri, 4.2465 light years away.
The travelling twin cruises at 99% of light speed both ways, and the turnaround is treated as instant.
A realistic 1 g accelerate-then-brake rocket trip is also worked out for comparison.
Both twins are 30 years old at departure.
Flat spacetime: gravity from the Sun and from Proxima is ignored.

d_ly = 2.537e6            # distance to Andromeda (M31), light years

t_e = r["t_earth_s"]; t_s = r["t_ship_s"]; d_ship = r["distance_ship_frame_m"]; ke = r["kinetic_energy_per_kg_J"]

t_s_yr = t_s / yr
d_ship_ly = d_ship / ly
lag_yr = (t_e - d / c) / yr

# Energy for a 1000 tonne ship
m_ship = 1.0e6
E_ship = ke * m_ship
world = 6.0e20

n_igm = 1.0   # protons per m^3 between galaxies
P_bow = n_igm * v * (gam - 1) * wie.m_p * c**2

T_cmb_ahead = wie.T_cmb * D
theta_side = np.degrees(np.arccos(beta))

# Getting up to speed at 1 g
rap = np.arctanh(beta)
tau_acc_yr = c * rap / wie.g0 / yr
x_acc_ly = c**2 / wie.g0 * (gam - 1) / ly
rk = wie.rocket(d, accel=wie.g0, flip=True)
tau_rocket_yr = rk["tau_total_s"] / yr
t_rocket_yr = rk["t_total_s"] / yr
tau_rocket_formula = 2 * c / wie.g0 * np.arccosh(1 + wie.g0 * (d / 2) / c**2) / yr

# Andromeda approaches at ~110 km/s; how much it closes during the trip
closing_ly = 110e3 * t_e / ly

# Scene in million light years
F = 220
t = np.linspace(0, t_e_yr, F)          # years, Earth clock
tM = t / 1e6
D_M = d_ly / 1e6
x_ship = v * t * yr / ly / 1e6
x_light = np.minimum(c * t * yr / ly / 1e6, D_M)

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
def disk(N, Rd, Rmax, incl, center):

    ph = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, N)

mw, Tmw = disk(900, 0.012, 0.06, 0.0, [0, 0, 0])

s.body("Ship", np.c_[x_ship, 0 * t, 0 * t + 0.03], radius=0.015, kind="ship", color="#e0e8ff",

s.body("Light flash from launch", np.c_[x_light, 0 * t, 0 * t - 0.03], radius=0.008, kind="light", color="#fff6a0")
s.curve("Route", np.array([[0, 0, 0], [D_M, 0, 0]]), color="#5577aa", width=0.6)

s.series("Ship clock", t / gam, "years")
s.series("Earth clock", t, "years")
s.series("Distance travelled", x_ship, "million ly")

s.number("Trip time on Earth's clock", t_e_yr, "years", f"light itself takes {d_ly:.4g} years")
s.number("Trip time on the ship's clock", t_s_yr, "years", "far longer than a human life")
s.number("Lorentz factor", gam, "", "clocks aboard run this many times slower")
s.number("Route length seen by the crew", d_ship_ly, "light years", "length contraction")

spec.question: What if gravity were 10 times weaker?

params.code:
import numpy as np
import wie
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

k = 0.1
G0 = wie.G
Gp = G0 * k
AU = wie.AU
day = wie.day
M = wie.M_sun
R0 = wie.R_sun
R_E = 6.371e6

def surface_g(Gval, Mb, R):
    return Gval * Mb / R**2

def esc_speed(Gval, Mb, r):
    return np.sqrt(2 * Gval * Mb / r)

# ---------- Lane-Emden n=3 polytrope for the Sun's structure ----------
def le(x, y):
    return [y[1], -max(y[0], 0.0)**3 - 2 * y[1] / x]
def hit(x, y):
    return y[0]
hit.terminal = True
hit.direction = -1
x0 = 1e-6
sol_le = solve_ivp(le, [x0, 20], [1 - x0**2 / 6, -x0 / 3], events=hit, dense_output=True, rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-13)
xi1 = sol_le.t_events[0][0] if len(sol_le.t_events[0]) > 0 else 6.89685
xi = np.linspace(x0, xi1, 6000)
th, dth = sol_le.sol(xi)
th = np.clip(th, 0, None)
mxi = -xi**2 * dth
m1 = mxi[-1]
q = mxi / m1
sfr = xi / xi1
dqds = np.gradient(q, sfr)
rho_ratio = xi1**3 / (3 * m1)                 # central / mean density
w_coef = np.trapezoid(q * dqds / sfr, sfr)    # |W| = w_coef G M^2 / R
beta = np.trapezoid(sfr**2 * dqds, sfr)       # sum r^2 dm = beta M R^2

W0 = w_coef * G0 * M**2 / R0                  # today's binding energy
U0 = 0.5 * W0                                 # virial thermal energy
Wp = k * W0                                   # binding after G drops
E_tot = U0 - Wp                               # > 0  => unbound
v_edge_inf = np.sqrt(2 * E_tot / (beta * M))

# ---------- homologous expansion of the Sun ----------
def sun_rhs(t, y):
    R, Rd = y
    return [Rd, (2 * U0 * R0**2 / R**3 - Wp * R0 / R**2) / (beta * M)]
def sun_acc_today(R):
    return (2 * U0 * R0**2 / R**3 - W0 * R0 / R**2) / (beta * M)

T_end = 20 * day
td_dense = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.geomspace(1.0, T_end, 30000)])
sd = wie.solve(sun_rhs, [R0, 0.0], td_dense)
Rt, Rdt = sd[:, 0], sd[:, 1]
E_end = 0.5 * beta * M * Rdt[-1]**2 + U0 * (R0 / Rt[-1])**2 - Wp * R0 / Rt[-1]
t_dyn = np.sqrt(R0**3 / (Gp * M))
i2 = np.argmax(Rt >= 2 * R0)
t_double = td_dense[i2]
Tc0 = 1.57e7
Tc_double = Tc0 * (R0 / Rt[i2])**2

def menc_frac(x):
    return np.where(x >= 1, 1.0, np.interp(x, sfr, q))

# ---------- Earth and Moon in the shrinking enclosed mass ----------
mE, mM = wie.M_earth, wie.M_moon
def f(t, y):
    pE = np.array(y[0:3]); pM = np.array(y[3:6])
    R = np.interp(t, td_dense, Rt)
    rE = np.linalg.norm(pE); rM = np.linalg.norm(pM)
    aE = -Gp * M * menc_frac(rE / R) * pE / rE**3
    aM = -Gp * M * menc_frac(rM / R) * pM / rM**3
    d = pM - pE; dn = np.linalg.norm(d)
    aE = aE + Gp * mM * d / dn**3
    aM = aM - Gp * mE * d / dn**3
    return np.concatenate([y[6:12], aE, aM])

v_earth = np.sqrt(G0 * M / AU)
v_moon_rel = 1022.0
y0 = [AU, 0, 0, AU + wie.a_moon, 0, 0, 0, v_earth, 0, 0, v_earth + v_moon_rel, 0]
t = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.geomspace(600.0, T_end, 239)])
so = wie.solve(f, y0, t)
pE = so[:, 0:3]; pM = so[:, 3:6]; vE = so[:, 6:9]
r_es = np.linalg.norm(pE, axis=1)
r_em = np.linalg.norm(pM - pE, axis=1)
v_final = np.linalg.norm(vE[-1])
vesc_sun_new = esc_speed(Gp, M, AU)

# ---------- solar gas sweeping over Earth ----------
rE_d = np.interp(td_dense, t, r_es)
x_d = rE_d / Rt
rho_c = rho_ratio * M / (4 / 3 * np.pi * Rt**3)
theta_d = np.where(x_d < 1, np.interp(x_d, sfr, th), 0.0)
rho_gas = rho_c * theta_d**3
v_gas = Rdt * np.minimum(x_d, 1.0)
P_ram = rho_gas * v_gas**2
ip = np.argmax(P_ram)
P_ram_max = P_ram[ip]
t_peak = td_dense[ip]
E_hit = np.trapezoid(0.5 * rho_gas * v_gas**3 * np.pi * R_E**2, td_dense)
i_arrive = np.argmax(Rt >= rE_d)
t_arrive = td_dense[i_arrive]
E_bind_earth_new = k * 2.49e32
E_sun_year = 1361.0 * np.pi * R_E**2 * wie.year

g_new = surface_g(Gp, wie.M_earth, R_E)
g_today = surface_g(G0, wie.M_earth, R_E)
jump_new = 0.5 * g_today / g_new

# ---------- scene ----------
F = len(t)
Rf = np.interp(t, td_dense, Rt)
s = wie.Scene(t / day, time_unit="days", length_unit="AU")
sun_pos = np.zeros((F, 3)); sun_pos[Rf > 3 * R0] = np.nan
s.body("Sun", sun_pos, radius=Rf / AU, kind="star", temperature=5772 * (R0 / Rf)**2)
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
N = 2400
qi = rng.random(N)
si = np.interp(qi, q, sfr)
dirs = rng.normal(size=(N, 3)); dirs /= np.linalg.norm(dirs, axis=1)[:, None]
cloud = dirs[None, :, :] * (si[None, :, None] * Rf[:, None, None] / AU)
thi = np.interp(si, sfr, th)
Tcl = np.maximum(Tcc := Tc0 * thi[None, :] * (R0 / Rf[:, None])**2, 30.0)
s.cloud("Solar gas", cloud, color="#ffcc66", size=1.0, temperature=Tcl)
s.body("Earth", pE / AU, radius=10 * R_E / AU, kind="earth", spin=2 * np.pi)
s.body("Moon", pM / AU, radius=10 * wie.R_moon / AU, kind="moon")
s.curve("Earth's path", pE / AU, color="#88ccff", width=1.5)
s.series("Sun's radius", Rf / R0, "R_sun")
s.series("Earth-Sun distance", r_es / AU, "AU")
s.series("Earth-Moon distance", r_em / 1e3, "km")

s.number("Surface gravity on Earth", g_new, "m/s^2", f"today {g_today:.2f} m/s^2; a 0.5 m jump goes {jump_new:.1f} m")
s.number("Sun's total energy after the change", E_tot, "J", "positive: gas pressure beats gravity, the Sun is unbound")
s.number("Final outer-edge speed of solar gas", v_edge_inf / 1e3, "km/s", "homologous n=3 polytrope model")
s.number("Time for solar gas to reach Earth", t_arrive / day, "days", "")
s.number("Peak gas ram pressure on Earth", P_ram_max / 101325, "atm", "pressure of the solar gas wind hitting Earth")
s.number("Gas kinetic energy hitting Earth", E_hit, "J", f"{E_hit/E_sun_year:.1e} years of today's sunlight; {E_hit/E_bind_earth_new:.1f}x Earth's weakened binding energy")

s.caption(0, f"G drops to 1/10. The Sun's hot gas still pushes out as before, but gravity holds it with a tenth of the force: total energy jumps to +{E_tot:.2e} J, so the Sun is unbound.")
s.caption(t_double / day, f"After {t_double/3600:.1f} hours the Sun has doubled in size and its core has cooled from 15.7 million K to {Tc_double/1e6:.1f} million K: fusion shuts off.")
s.caption(t_arrive / day, f"After {t_arrive/day:.1f} days the expanding gas reaches Earth. Earth's orbit is gone anyway: at 1 AU the escape speed is now only {vesc_sun_new/1e3:.2f} km/s, versus Earth's {v_earth/1e3:.2f} km/s.")
s.caption(t_peak / day, f"The solar wind of the dead Sun hits Earth with up to {P_ram_max/101325:.0f} atm of ram pressure, carrying {E_hit:.1e} J into Earth's cross-section, enough to strip the air and scorch the surface.")
s.caption(T_end / day, f"After 20 days Earth coasts at {v_final/1e3:.1f} km/s through cold, dark space {r_es[-1]/AU:.2f} AU from where the Sun was; the Moon has drifted {r_em[-1]/1e3:,.0f} km away.")

s.check("Lane-Emden n=3 binding coefficient equals 3/(5-n)", w_coef, 1.5, rtol=2e-3)
s.check("Sun expansion conserves energy", E_end, E_tot, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Sun's edge reaches the analytic asymptotic speed", Rdt[-1], v_edge_inf, rtol=2e-2)
s.check("Baseline: with today's G the model Sun is in equilibrium (zero acceleration)", sun_acc_today(R0) / surface_g(G0, M, R0), 0.0, atol=1e-9)
s.check("Baseline: n=3 central to mean density ratio matches textbook 54.18", rho_ratio, 54.18, rtol=2e-3)
s.check("Baseline: today's surface gravity matches measured 9.81 m/s^2", g_today, 9.81, rtol=3e-3)

s.answer(f"If gravity were 10 times weaker you would weigh a tenth as much (g = {g_new:.2f} m/s^2), but the Sun could not survive: its hot gas, no longer held in, would fly apart, and within {t_double/3600:.1f} hours it would double in size and stop fusing. Its gas would reach Earth after {t_arrive/day:.1f} days with a ram pressure of up to {P_ram_max/101325:.0f} atm, carrying {E_hit:.1e} J of kinetic energy into Earth. Earth and the Moon would no longer orbit anything and would coast off into the dark, Earth at {v_final/1e3:.1f} km/s.")
s.camera(focus="Earth", view="top")

assumptions: G drops to one tenth instantly everywhere; masses, temperatures and speeds are unchanged at that moment.
The Sun is modelled as an n=3 polytrope in virial equilibrium that expands homologously and adiabatically (gamma 5/3); radiation pressure and shocks are ignored.
Earth stays intact because rock strength, not gravity, holds it at these scales; atmospheric loss and surface heating are not modelled in detail.
How much of the gas energy actually couples into Earth is uncertain; the figure given is what passes through Earth's cross-section.
The Sun's centre of mass stays fixed; other planets are left out because they barely affect Earth over 20 days.
Earth and Moon are drawn 10 times their true size so they are visible.

import numpy as np
import wie

c = wie.c
a = wie.g0
yr = wie.year
tau_end = 10 * yr
L = c**2 / a

F = 240
tau = np.linspace(0, tau_end, F)
phi = a * tau / c
t_e = (c / a) * np.sinh(phi)
x = L * (np.cosh(phi) - 1)
gam = np.cosh(phi)
one_minus_beta = 2.0 / (np.exp(2 * phi) + 1)

phi_end = phi[-1]
t_end_yr = t_e[-1] / yr
x_end_ly = x[-1] / wie.ly
gam_end = gam[-1]
shortfall = c * one_minus_beta[-1]
ke_per_kg = (gam_end - 1) * c**2
mass_ratio_photon = np.exp(phi_end)

ph_half = a * 5 * yr / c
x_flip_ly = 2 * L * (np.cosh(ph_half) - 1) / wie.ly
t_flip_yr = 2 * (c / a) * np.sinh(ph_half) / yr

# independent check: Earth-frame hyperbolic motion, integrate dt/gamma over a fine Earth-time grid
tt = np.linspace(0, t_e[-1], 400001)
gam_t = np.sqrt(1 + (a * tt / c)**2)
tau_from_int = np.trapezoid(1.0 / gam_t, tt)
hyper = (x[-1] + L)**2 - (c * t_e[-1])**2

tau_yr = tau / yr
s = wie.Scene(tau_yr, time_unit="ship years", length_unit="light years")
xl = x / wie.ly
s.body("Earth", [0, 0, 0], radius=150, kind="earth")
s.body("Ship", np.c_[xl, 0 * xl, 0 * xl], radius=150, kind="ship", color="#e0e8ff",
       scale=np.c_[np.clip(1 / gam, 0.05, 1), np.ones(F), np.ones(F)])
s.curve("Path", np.c_[xl, 0 * xl, 0 * xl], color="#66ccff", width=1.0)
s.body("Orion Nebula (1,344 ly)", [1344, 600, 0], radius=120, kind="star", temperature=30000)
s.body("Crab Nebula (6,500 ly)", [6500, -700, 0], radius=120, kind="star", temperature=12000)
s.body("Galactic Centre direction (26,000 ly)", [26000, 0, 0], radius=300, kind="star", temperature=4500)

s.series("Earth time elapsed", t_e / yr, "years")
s.series("Distance from Earth", xl, "light years")
s.series("Lorentz factor", gam, "")

s.number("Earth time after 10 ship years", t_end_yr, "years", "Time that passes on Earth while the crew ages 10 years")
s.number("Distance travelled (Earth frame)", x_end_ly, "light years", "Over half way to the galactic centre")
s.number("Final Lorentz factor", gam_end, "", "How much slower ship clocks tick than Earth's")
s.number("Final shortfall below light speed", shortfall, "m/s", "c minus the ship's speed")
s.number("Photon-drive mass ratio", mass_ratio_photon, "", "Starting mass per kg of payload, perfect photon drive")
s.number("Accelerate 5 yr, brake 5 yr: distance", x_flip_ly, "light years", f"arriving at rest after {t_flip_yr:.0f} Earth years")

i1 = np.searchsorted(tau_yr, 1.0)
s.caption(0, "Engines on: a steady 1 g, so the crew feel normal Earth weight for the whole trip.")
s.caption(1.0, f"After 1 ship year the rocket is at {np.tanh(phi[i1])*100:.1f}% of light speed and {xl[i1]:.2f} light years out.")
s.caption(3.0, "Speed creeps towards c but never reaches it. Time dilation keeps growing, so each ship year covers more and more light years.")
s.caption(6.0, f"By the end every kilogram of payload carries {ke_per_kg:.2e} J of kinetic energy, so a perfect photon drive needs {mass_ratio_photon:.0f} kg of starting mass per kg of payload.")
s.caption(10.0, f"Ten ship years: {t_end_yr:.0f} years have passed on Earth, the ship is {x_end_ly:.0f} light years away and only {shortfall:.2f} m/s slower than light. Lorentz factor {gam_end:.0f}.")

s.check("Baseline: Newtonian limit, speed after 1 hour at 1 g equals g*t", c * np.tanh(a * 3600.0 / c), 9.80665 * 3600, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Proper time integrated in Earth frame equals 10 years", tau_from_int, tau_end, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Worldline is the hyperbola (x + c^2/a)^2 - (ct)^2 = (c^2/a)^2", hyper, L**2, rtol=1e-8)

s.answer(f"If a rocket kept up 1 g for 10 years by its own clock, it would travel {x_end_ly:.0f} light years, more than half way to the galactic centre, while {t_end_yr:.0f} years pass on Earth. By the end it is only {shortfall:.2f} m/s slower than light, with a Lorentz factor of {gam_end:.0f}. Even a perfect photon drive would need {mass_ratio_photon:.0f} kg of starting mass per kg of payload. To stop at the destination instead, accelerating for 5 years and braking for 5 gets you {x_flip_ly:.0f} light years away.")

import numpy as np
import wie

d = 100 * wie.ly
t_light = d / wie.c
t_light_yr = t_light / wie.year

def app_mag(M_abs, dist_m):
    return M_abs + 5 * np.log10((dist_m / wie.pc) / 10.0)

M_sun_abs = 4.83          # Sun's absolute V magnitude
m_sun = app_mag(M_sun_abs, d)
p_geo = 0.367             # Earth's geometric albedo
contrast = p_geo * (wie.R_earth / wie.AU) ** 2   # Earth/Sun flux ratio at full phase
dimmer = 1.0 / contrast
m_earth = m_sun - 2.5 * np.log10(contrast)

sep = np.arctan(wie.AU / d)
sep_mas = sep * 206264.806 * 1000
theta_E = 2 * wie.R_earth / d
lam = 550e-9
D_disk_km = 1.22 * lam / theta_E / 1000
D_split_m = 1.22 * lam / sep

F_sun = wie.L_sun / (4 * np.pi * d ** 2)
F_earth = contrast * F_sun
A_tel = np.pi * 5.0 ** 2
phot_rate = F_earth * A_tel / (wie.h * wie.c / lam)

# scene
F = 300
t = np.linspace(0, 100, F)
Rd = 3.0
earth = np.c_[Rd * np.cos(2 * np.pi * t), Rd * np.sin(2 * np.pi * t), 0 * t]
s = wie.Scene(t, time_unit="years since the light left", length_unit="light years")
s.body("Sun", [0, 0, 0], radius=0.8, kind="star", temperature=5772)
s.body("Earth", earth, radius=0.4, kind="earth")
s.body("Observer telescope", [100.0, 0, 0], radius=1.0, kind="ship", color="#cccccc")
s.body("Light leaving Earth", np.c_[t, 0 * t, 0 * t], radius=0.6, kind="light", color="#9fd3ff")
N = 900
i = np.arange(N) + 0.5
phi = np.arccos(1 - 2 * i / N)
th = np.pi * (1 + 5 ** 0.5) * i
u = np.c_[np.cos(th) * np.sin(phi), np.sin(th) * np.sin(phi), np.cos(phi)]
shell = t[:, None, None] * u[None, :, :]
s.cloud("Expanding light shell", shell, color="#7fbfff", size=0.6)
beam = np.zeros((F, 2, 3))
beam[:, 1, 0] = t
s.curve("Light path", beam, color="#9fd3ff", width=1.0)
s.series("Light front distance", t, "ly")
s.series("Distance still to go", 100 - t, "ly")

s.number("Light travel time", t_light_yr, "years", "You see Earth as it was this long ago")
s.number("Sun's apparent magnitude", m_sun, "mag", "Naked-eye limit is about 6.5, so the Sun is invisible without binoculars")
s.number("Earth's apparent magnitude (full phase)", m_earth, "mag", "Only the largest telescopes reach this faint")
s.number("Earth fainter than the Sun by", dimmer, "times", "Reflected light only, full phase")
s.number("Earth-Sun separation on the sky", sep_mas, "milliarcseconds", "About a hair's width seen from 600 m")
s.number("Telescope needed to see Earth as a disk", D_disk_km, "km", "Diffraction limit at 550 nm")
s.number("Photons from Earth into a 10 m telescope", phot_rate, "per second", "Approximate, all treated as 550 nm light")

s.caption(0, f"Light leaves Earth. It will take {t_light_yr:.0f} years to cross 100 light years, so the observer sees a world {t_light_yr:.0f} years in its past (Earth's orbit drawn hugely enlarged)")
s.caption(25, f"From there the Sun shrinks to a magnitude {m_sun:.1f} star, too faint to see with the naked eye")
s.caption(50, f"Earth is {dimmer:.1e} times fainter than the Sun, at magnitude {m_earth:.1f}, and sits only {sep_mas:.1f} milliarcseconds from it")
s.caption(75, f"Splitting Earth from the Sun needs only a {D_split_m:.1f} m mirror in principle, but seeing Earth as a disk needs a {D_disk_km:.0f} km telescope")
s.caption(100, f"The light arrives: a 10 m telescope would catch about {phot_rate:.0f} photons per second from Earth, showing a pale dot from {t_light_yr:.0f} years ago, before television existed")

s.check("Baseline: Sun's apparent magnitude from 1 AU matches measured -26.74", app_mag(M_sun_abs, wie.AU), -26.74, rtol=3e-3)

import wie

AU = wie.AU; ly = wie.ly; yr = wie.year; c = wie.c
L = wie.L_sun; M = wie.M_sun; sig = wie.sigma_SB
albedo = 0.30

def t_eq(r, q=0.0): return ((flux(r) * (1 - albedo) / 4 + q) / sig) ** 0.25
def period(r): return 2 * np.pi * np.sqrt(r**3 / (wie.G * M))
def v_circ(r): return np.sqrt(wie.G * M / r)
def mag(r): return -26.74 + 5 * np.log10(r / AU)

r_new = c * yr            # distance light covers in one year
r_ly = r_new / ly
ratio = r_new / AU
S_new = flux(r_new); S_now = flux(AU)
T_sun_only = t_eq(r_new)
T_new = t_eq(r_new, q_geo)
T_now = t_eq(AU)
P_new_yr = period(r_new) / yr
v_new = v_circ(r_new) / 1e3
m_new = mag(r_new)
dim_factor = S_now / S_new
g_sun_new = wie.G * M / r_new**2

# scene: one year of a light flash travelling out from the Sun
F = 220
t = np.linspace(0, 1.3 * light_time(r_new) / yr, F)
s = wie.Scene(t, time_unit="years", length_unit="light years")
s.body("Sun", [0, 0, 0], radius=0.04, kind="star", temperature=5772)
ang = 2 * np.pi * t / P_new_yr
s.body("Earth", np.c_[r_ly * np.cos(ang), r_ly * np.sin(ang), 0 * t], radius=0.03,
       kind="earth", temperature=T_new, spin=2 * np.pi * 365.25)
th = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
s.curve("Earth's new orbit (one lap = %.1f million years)" % (P_new_yr / 1e6),
        np.c_[r_ly * np.cos(th), r_ly * np.sin(th), 0 * th], color="#5577aa", width=0.6)

# expanding shell of light emitted at t=0, moving at c = 1 ly/yr
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
N = 2000
u = rng.normal(size=(N, 3)); u /= np.linalg.norm(u, axis=1)[:, None]
u[:, 2] *= 0.3
u /= np.linalg.norm(u, axis=1)[:, None]

s.series("Distance travelled by the flash", R, "light years")
s.series("Earth temperature", np.full(F, T_new), "K")

s.number("Sunlight at Earth", S_new, "W/m²", f"{dim_factor:.2e} times dimmer than today's {S_now:.0f} W/m²")

params.code:
import numpy as np
import wie

c = wie.c
beta = 0.99
v0 = beta * c
M = 1500.0          # car mass kg
A = 2.2             # frontal area m^2
rho = 1.225         # sea-level air density kg/m^3
u = 1.66053906660e-27

def gm1(vel):
    # gamma - 1 in a cancellation-free form
    b2 = (vel / c) ** 2
    sq = np.sqrt(1.0 - b2)
    return b2 / (sq * (1.0 + sq))

def ke(mass, vel):
    return gm1(vel) * mass * c**2

gamma = wie.lorentz(v0)
KE = ke(M, v0)
KE_mt = KE / 4.184e15
tsar = KE_mt / 50.0
E_N2_GeV = (gamma - 1) * 28 * u * c**2 / (1e9 * wie.e_charge)
P0 = rho * A * v0 * (gamma - 1) * c**2
P_sun = P0 / wie.L_sun
v_esc = np.sqrt(2 * wie.G * wie.M_earth / wie.R_earth)
esc_ratio = v0 / v_esc
t_vap = 1500.0 * 7e6 / P0   # ~7 MJ/kg to heat and vaporise steel

# relativistic snowplough: car+swept air move together, E and p conserved
E0 = gamma * M * c**2
p = gamma * M * beta * c
k = rho * A * c**2
def x_at_speed(bf):
    return (p * c / bf - E0) / k
x_half = x_at_speed(0.5)
x_end = x_at_speed(0.1)
def t_of_x(x):
    return (E0 * x + 0.5 * k * x**2) / (p * c**2)
t_half = t_of_x(x_half)
t_end = t_of_x(x_end)
m_sw_end = rho * A * x_end
Mi_end = np.sqrt((E0 + k * x_end)**2 - (p * c)**2) / c**2
heat_end = (Mi_end - M - m_sw_end) * c**2
heat_frac = heat_end / KE

F = 240
t = np.linspace(0, t_end, F)
x = (-E0 + np.sqrt(E0**2 + 2 * k * p * c**2 * t)) / k
sol = wie.solve(lambda tt, y: [p * c**2 / (E0 + k * y[0])], [0.0], t)
vb = p * c / (E0 + k * x)

us = t * 1e6
xk = x / 1e3
s = wie.Scene(us, time_unit="microseconds", length_unit="km")
carpos = np.full((F, 3), np.nan)
carpos[0] = [0, 0, 0]
s.body("Car", carpos, radius=0.05, kind="ship", color="#cc2222", scale=[1 / gamma, 1, 1])
s.body("Plasma front", np.c_[xk, 0 * xk, 0 * xk], radius=0.4, kind="generic", color="#bfe6ff", temperature=20000)

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
N = 2400
xh = np.sort(rng.uniform(0, x_end, N))
th = t_of_x(xh)
phi = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, N)
fr = rng.uniform(0.2, 1.0, N)
vexp = 0.5 * c
pts = np.zeros((F, N, 3))
for i in range(F):
    hit = th <= t[i]
    r = np.where(hit, fr * vexp * (t[i] - th), 0.0) / 1e3
    px = np.where(hit, xh / 1e3, xk[i] - 0.2 * fr)
    rr = np.where(hit, r, 0.2 * fr)
    pts[i, :, 0] = px
    pts[i, :, 1] = rr * np.cos(phi)
    pts[i, :, 2] = rr * np.sin(phi)
s.cloud("Shocked air and car plasma", pts, color="#ffd27a", size=1.5, temperature=20000)
s.curve("Road", np.array([[0, 0, -0.5], [x_end / 1e3, 0, -0.5]]), color="#555555", width=0.5)

s.series("Plasma front speed", vb, "c")
s.series("Distance travelled", xk, "km")

s.number("Lorentz factor", gamma, "", "Car clocks run this much slower; its length shrinks by the same factor")
s.number("Kinetic energy of a 1500 kg car", KE_mt, "megatons TNT", f"{KE:.2e} J, about {tsar:.0f} Tsar Bombas (50 Mt each)")
s.number("Power dumped into air at the start", P_sun, "Suns", f"{P0:.2e} W versus the Sun's luminosity")
s.number("Energy of each N2 molecule hit", E_N2_GeV, "GeV", "Particle-accelerator collisions, trillions per second")
s.number("Distance to slow to half light speed", x_half, "m", f"reached after {t_half*1e6:.2f} microseconds")
s.number("Distance to slow to 10% of light speed", x_end / 1e3, "km", f"after {t_end*1e6:.0f} microseconds")

s.caption(0, f"At 99% of light speed the Lorentz factor is {gamma:.2f}; the car carries {KE_mt:.0f} megatons TNT of kinetic energy")
s.caption(us[1], f"Every air molecule strikes at {E_N2_GeV:.0f} GeV; the car vaporises in about {t_vap:.0e} s, long before it moves a hair")
s.caption(us[F // 8], f"The air is being heated at {P0:.2e} W, {P_sun:.1f} times the Sun's entire output")
s.caption(t_half * 1e6, f"The plasma plough of car and air has slowed to half light speed after only {x_half:.0f} m")
s.caption(us[F // 2], f"It is {esc_ratio:.0f} times Earth's escape speed, but it never reaches space: the air stops it first")
s.caption(t_end * 1e6, f"After {x_end/1e3:.1f} km it is down to 10% of light speed; {heat_frac*100:.0f}% of the energy is already heat: a giant fireball")

s.check("ODE path matches analytic snowplough solution", sol[-1, 0], x[-1], rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Lorentz factor equals 1/sqrt(1-b^2)", gamma, 1 / np.sqrt(1 - beta**2), rtol=1e-12)
s.check("Stable gamma-1 matches direct form at 0.99c", gm1(v0), gamma - 1, rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Newtonian limit: KE -> mv^2/2 at 100 km/h", ke(M, 27.78), 0.5 * M * 27.78**2, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Baseline: near-light-speed travel time Sun to Earth equals sunlight's measured 499 s", wie.AU / ((1 - 1e-12) * c), 499.0, rtol=2e-3)

s.answer(f"A 1500 kg car at 99% of light speed has a Lorentz factor of {gamma:.2f} and carries {KE_mt:.0f} megatons TNT of kinetic energy, about {tsar:.0f} Tsar Bombas (50 Mt each). The moment it moves, every air molecule hits it at {E_N2_GeV:.0f} GeV, dumping energy {P_sun:.1f} times faster than the Sun shines, so the car turns to plasma almost instantly. That plasma ploughs on, slowing to half light speed after {x_half:.0f} m and to 10% of light speed after {x_end/1e3:.1f} km, leaving an explosion far bigger than any nuclear weapon ever built.")
s.camera(focus="Plasma front", view="side")

assumptions: Car of 1500 kg with 2.2 m^2 frontal area, starting at 99% of light speed in sea-level air of 1.225 kg/m^3.
How it reached that speed is ignored; it is simply given that speed.
Car and swept-up air are treated as one blob that conserves total energy and momentum (relativistic snowplough).
Real air would partly stream through and spread out sideways, so the slowing distances are order-of-magnitude estimates.
Sideways growth of the fireball at half light speed is only a visual guide, not a computed result.
Steel takes about 7 MJ/kg to heat and vaporise, which sets the rough vaporisation time.
Earth's curvature and the ground are ignored over the short path.
The car is drawn larger than real scale so it stays visible.

import numpy as np
import wie
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

G, c = wie.G, wie.c
M = wie.M_earth
R = wie.R_earth
GM = G * M
r_s = 2 * GM / c**2
bh = wie.black_hole(M)
T_H = bh["hawking_temperature_K"]
t_evap_yr = bh["evaporation_time_years"]

# --- Collapse: pressure switched off, uniform dust sphere falls in (Oppenheimer-Snyder / Newtonian dust) ---
tau0 = np.sqrt(R**3 / (2 * GM))
t_ff = 0.5 * np.pi * tau0
eta = np.linspace(0, 0.5 * np.pi, 40000)
t_eta = (eta + np.sin(eta) * np.cos(eta)) * tau0
f_eta = np.cos(eta) ** 2
def shrink(t):
    return np.where(t < t_ff, np.interp(t, t_eta, f_eta), 0.0)

# numerical check of the surface fall time to r = 1e-3 R
def rad(t, y):
    return [y[1], -GM / y[0] ** 2]
def ev(t, y):
    return y[0] - 1e-3 * R
ev.terminal = True
sol_c = solve_ivp(rad, [0, 2 * t_ff], [R, 0.0], method="DOP853", rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-6, events=ev)
t_num = sol_c.t_events[0][0] if len(sol_c.t_events[0]) > 0 else np.nan
eta_k = np.arccos(np.sqrt(1e-3))
t_ana = (eta_k + np.sin(eta_k) * np.cos(eta_k)) * tau0

# --- Moon: orbit set by mass alone, so unchanged ---
GMt = G * (M + wie.M_moon)
a = wie.a_moon
v0 = np.sqrt(GMt / a)
P = 2 * np.pi * np.sqrt(a**3 / GMt)

t1 = np.linspace(0, 0.999 * t_ff, 90)
t2 = np.geomspace(1.02 * t_ff, 2 * P, 160)
t = np.concatenate([t1, t2])
F = len(t)
def orb(tt, y):
    r3 = (y[0]**2 + y[1]**2) ** 1.5
    return [y[2], y[3], -GMt * y[0] / r3, -GMt * y[1] / r3]
sm = wie.solve(orb, [a, 0.0, 0.0, v0], t)
moon = np.c_[sm[:, 0], sm[:, 1], 0 * t] / 1e3
E0 = 0.5 * v0**2 - GMt / a
Ef = 0.5 * (sm[-1, 2]**2 + sm[-1, 3]**2) - GMt / np.hypot(sm[-1, 0], sm[-1, 1])

# --- Physics headline numbers ---
g_surface = GM / R**2
g_1m = GM / 1.0**2
v_esc_old = np.sqrt(2 * GM / R)
rho_bh = M / (4 / 3 * np.pi * r_s**3)
P_hawk = wie.hbar * c**6 / (15360 * np.pi * G**2 * M**2)
P_cmb = wie.sigma_SB * wie.T_cmb**4 * (27 / 4) * np.pi * r_s**2
d_tear = (2 * GM * 2.0 / 1000.0) ** (1 / 3)  # 2 m body feels 1000 m/s^2 stretch
tid_tear = wie.tidal_acceleration(M, d_tear, 2.0)

th = t / 3600.0
s = wie.Scene(th, time_unit="h", length_unit="km")

# Earth shown only at the start; then its matter is a falling cloud
earth_pos = np.full((F, 3), np.nan); earth_pos[0] = 0.0
s.body("Earth", earth_pos, radius=R / 1e3, kind="earth")
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
N = 2500
u = rng.normal(size=(N, 3)); u /= np.linalg.norm(u, axis=1)[:, None]
r0 = R * rng.random(N) ** (1 / 3)
pts0 = u * r0[:, None] / 1e3
fr = shrink(t)
s.cloud("Collapsing Earth matter", fr[:, None, None] * pts0[None], color="#b08a60", size=1.2)

bh_pos = np.full((F, 3), np.nan); bh_pos[t >= t_ff] = 0.0
s.body("Earth-mass black hole", bh_pos, radius=r_s / 1e3, kind="blackhole", disk=False)
s.body("Moon", moon, radius=wie.R_moon / 1e3, kind="moon")
ang = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 300)
s.curve("Moon's orbit (unchanged)", np.c_[a * np.cos(ang), a * np.sin(ang), 0 * ang] / 1e3, color="#8899ff", width=0.6)

s.series("Radius of Earth's matter", np.maximum(fr * R, r_s) / 1e3, "km")
s.series("Moon distance", np.hypot(sm[:, 0], sm[:, 1]) / 1e3, "km")

s.number("Schwarzschild radius", r_s * 1e3, "mm", "All of Earth's mass inside a sphere about the size of a marble")
s.number("Free-fall collapse time", t_ff / 60, "min", "If nothing held Earth up")
s.number("Moon's orbital period", P / wie.day, "days", "Unchanged: the Moon only feels Earth's mass")
s.number("Hawking temperature", T_H, "K", "Colder than the 2.725 K cosmic background, so it grows instead of evaporating")
s.number("Gravity 1 m from the black hole", g_1m, "m/s^2", f"vs {g_surface:.2f} m/s^2 at the old surface radius")
s.number("Mean density inside the horizon", rho_bh, "kg/m^3", "")

s.caption(0, f"Switch off what holds Earth up: its {M:.2e} kg of rock falls inward and would collapse in {t_ff/60:.1f} min.")
s.caption(th[45], f"Everything falls together; at the old surface radius gravity is still {g_surface:.2f} m/s^2, escape speed {v_esc_old/1e3:.1f} km/s.")
s.caption(th[90], f"A black hole forms with Schwarzschild radius {r_s*1e3:.2f} mm and mean density {rho_bh:.1e} kg/m^3.")
s.caption(th[140], f"The Moon doesn't notice: same mass, same pull, it keeps its {P/wie.day:.2f} day orbit at {a/1e3:.0f} km. Ocean tides and eclipses of the Moon by Earth are gone.")
s.caption(th[200], f"Up close it is brutal: {g_1m:.1e} m/s^2 at 1 m, and a person would be torn apart within {d_tear/1e3:.0f} km of it.")
s.caption(th[-1], f"Its Hawking temperature is only {T_H:.4f} K. It absorbs about {P_cmb:.1e} W of background light but emits only {P_hawk:.1e} W, so for now it slowly grows.")

s.check("Surface fall time: numerical ODE vs cycloid formula", t_num, t_ana, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Schwarzschild radius matches 2GM/c^2 from helper", bh["r_s_m"], r_s, rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Moon orbital energy conserved", Ef, E0, rtol=1e-8)
s.check("Baseline: Moon's sidereal month (27.32 d)", P / wie.day, 27.32, rtol=0.01)
s.check("Baseline: surface gravity today (9.81 m/s^2)", g_surface, 9.81, rtol=0.01)
s.check("Baseline: Earth's published Schwarzschild radius (8.87 mm)", r_s * 1e3, 8.87, rtol=0.01)

Rc = 3.48e6; Mc = 1.94e24
rho_c = Mc / (4/3*np.pi*Rc**3)
rho_m = (Me - Mc) / (4/3*np.pi*(R**3 - Rc**3))
def menc(r):
    r = abs(r)
    if r < Rc:
        return rho_c*4/3*np.pi*r**3
    if r < R:
        return Mc + rho_m*4/3*np.pi*(r**3 - Rc**3)
    return Me
def rho_of(z):
    r = np.abs(z)
    return np.where(r < Rc, rho_c, np.where(r < R, rho_m, 0.0))
def g_layer(z):
    r = abs(z)
    if r < 1.0:
        return 0.0
    return -G*menc(r)/r**2*np.sign(z)

z0 = 3 * R
v0 = np.sqrt(v_inf**2 + 2*G*Me/z0)
def f(t, y): return [y[1], g_layer(y[0])]
def ev_in(t, y): return y[0] - R
def ev_c(t, y): return y[0]
def ev_out(t, y): return y[0] + R
sol = solve_ivp(f, [0, 600], [z0, -v0], rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-6, max_step=0.5,
                dense_output=True, events=[ev_in, ev_c, ev_out])
t_in = sol.t_events[0][0] if len(sol.t_events[0]) else np.nan
t_c = sol.t_events[1][0] if len(sol.t_events[1]) else np.nan
t_out = sol.t_events[2][0] if len(sol.t_events[2]) else np.nan
t_cross = t_out - t_in
v_c_num = abs(sol.sol(t_c)[1])
v_surf = abs(sol.sol(t_in)[1])

# analytic centre speed from the potential
k = 4/3*np.pi
core_part = G*rho_c*k*Rc**2/2
mant_part = G*(Mc - rho_m*k*Rc**3)*(1/Rc - 1/R) + G*rho_m*k*(R**2 - Rc**2)/2
v_c_an = np.sqrt(v_inf**2 + 2*G*Me/R + 2*(core_part + mant_part))

# energy deposit and accretion along the path
tt = np.linspace(t_in, t_out, 6000)
yy = sol.sol(tt)
zz, vv = yy[0], np.abs(yy[1])
rho = rho_of(zz)
lnL = np.log(R * vv**2 / GM)
dEdx = 4*np.pi*G**2*M**2*rho*lnL/vv**2
E_cum = np.concatenate([[0.0], cumulative_trapezoid(dEdx*vv, tt)])
E_tot = E_cum[-1]
MT = 4.184e15
E_Mt = E_tot / MT
t_per_m = (E_tot / (2*R)) / 4.184e9   # tonnes of TNT per metre
dMdt = 4*np.pi*G**2*M**2*rho/vv**3
M_acc = np.trapezoid(dMdt, tt)
KE = 0.5*M*v_c_num**2
frac_E = E_tot / KE
e_vap = 1.5e7
r_tun = np.sqrt((E_tot/(2*R))/e_vap/(np.pi*rho_m))
r_g = np.sqrt(GM / wie.g0)
dv_1km = 2*GM/(1e3*v_c_num)
c_p = 10e3
mach_deg = np.degrees(np.arcsin(c_p/v_c_num))

# frames
F = 240
T_end = t_out + 150
t = np.linspace(0, T_end, F)
zh = sol.sol(t)[0] / R
s = wie.Scene(t, time_unit="s", length_unit="Earth radii")
s.body("Primordial black hole", np.c_[0*t, 0*t, zh], radius=0.02, kind="blackhole", disk=False)

th = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 300)
s.curve("Earth surface", np.c_[np.sin(th), 0*th, np.cos(th)], color="#3a7bd5", width=2)
s.curve("Iron core", np.c_[Rc/R*np.sin(th), 0*th, Rc/R*np.cos(th)], color="#ff8833", width=1.5)

# pass time as a function of height (z decreasing in time)
zi = zz / R
def t_pass(zq):
    return np.interp(-zq, -zi, tt)

# vaporised tunnel cloud
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
N = 2200
zp = rng.uniform(-0.999, 0.999, N)
ang = rng.uniform(0, 2*np.pi, N)
rr = 0.006*np.sqrt(rng.uniform(0, 1, N))
tp = t_pass(zp)
pts = np.zeros((F, N, 3))
for i in range(F):
    done = t[i] >= tp
    pts[i, :, 0] = np.where(done, rr*np.cos(ang), 0.0)
    pts[i, :, 1] = np.where(done, rr*np.sin(ang), 0.0)
    pts[i, :, 2] = np.where(done, zp, zh[i])
s.cloud("Vaporised rock tunnel", pts, color="#ffaa44", size=1.0, temperature=4000.0)

# seismic Mach cone (envelope of P-wave spheres emitted along the path)
P = 200
zq = np.linspace(0.999, -0.999, P)
tq = t_pass(zq)
right = np.zeros((F, P, 3)); left = np.zeros((F, P, 3))
for i in range(F):
    rad = np.clip(c_p*(t[i]-tq)/R, 0, None)
    rad = np.minimum(rad, np.sqrt(1 - zq**2))
    passed = t[i] >= tq
    zc = np.where(passed, zq, np.clip(zh[i], -1, 1))
    right[i, :, 0] = np.where(passed, rad, 0.0); right[i, :, 2] = zc
    left[i, :, 0] = np.where(passed, -rad, 0.0); left[i, :, 2] = zc
s.curve("Seismic shock front", right, color="#ff4466", width=1.2)
s.curve("Seismic shock front (other side)", left, color="#ff4466", width=1.2)

speed = np.abs(sol.sol(t)[1]) / 1e3
s.series("Speed of the black hole", speed, "km/s")
s.series("Energy dumped into Earth", np.interp(t, tt, E_cum, left=0.0, right=E_tot)/MT, "Mt TNT")

s.number("Time to cross Earth", t_cross, "s", "Surface to surface, straight through the centre")
s.number("Energy deposited in Earth", E_Mt, "Mt TNT", "Gravitational dynamical friction along the 12,700 km path")
s.number("Black hole horizon radius", r_s*1e9, "nm", "1e19 kg, about the mass of a 200 km asteroid")
s.number("Mass swallowed (upper bound)", M_acc, "kg", "Hoyle-Lyttleton rate. Real rock gives less")
s.number("Hawking temperature", T_H, "K", f"Radiates only {P_hawk*1e6:.1f} microwatts")
s.number("Distance where its pull beats Earth's gravity", r_g/1e3, "km", "Only for a few hundredths of a second")

s.caption(0, f"A {M:.0e} kg primordial black hole, only {r_s*1e9:.0f} nm across, falls toward Earth at {v_inf/1e3:.0f} km/s")
s.caption(t_in, f"It enters at {v_surf/1e3:.1f} km/s. Earth's gravity barely speeds it up. It drills through rock, leaving about {t_per_m:.1f} tonnes of TNT of energy per metre")
s.caption(t_c, f"Centre crossed at {v_c_num/1e3:.1f} km/s. Rock within {r_g/1e3:.1f} km is pulled harder than by Earth, and rock 1 km away is kicked at {dv_1km:.1f} m/s")
s.caption(t_out, f"It exits after {t_cross:.1f} s, having dumped {E_Mt:.0f} Mt TNT into Earth. That is only {frac_E:.1e} of its kinetic energy, so it barely slows")
s.caption(t_out+60, f"A seismic Mach cone with a half-angle of {mach_deg:.1f} degrees spreads out, a vaporised tunnel at most {2*r_tun:.0f} m wide is left behind, and it swallowed at most {M_acc:.1e} kg")

s.check("Centre speed from integration matches the analytic potential", v_c_num, v_c_an, rtol=1e-5)
s.check("Crossing time close to the straight-line limit 2R/v_inf", t_cross, 2*R/v_inf, rtol=0.01)
s.check("Hawking temperature scales from the published 6.17e-8 K for one solar mass", T_H*M/wie.M_sun, 6.17e-8, rtol=0.01)
s.check("Baseline: surface gravity of the layered Earth vs measured 9.81 m/s^2", abs(g_layer(R*0.99999999)), 9.81, rtol=0.01)

s.answer(f"A {M:.0e} kg primordial black hole, smaller than a virus at {r_s*1e9:.0f} nm across, would punch straight through Earth in {t_cross:.1f} s at about {v_c_num/1e3:.1f} km/s and fly out the other side almost unaffected. "
         f"Its gravity would drag on the rock as it passed, dumping about {E_Mt:.0f} Mt TNT of energy along a thin tunnel. That would make a global seismic signal, but no catastrophe at the surface. "
         f"It would swallow at most {M_acc:.1e} kg of Earth, and its Hawking glow at {T_H:.0f} K is far too faint to matter.")
s.camera(focus=None, view="side")

assumptions: The primordial black hole has 1e19 kg, about the mass of a 200 km asteroid. It sits inside the range where primordial black holes could still be dark matter.
It arrives at 250 km/s, a typical speed for dark matter in our Galaxy, and travels straight through Earth's centre.
Earth is modelled as two layers: a uniform iron core of radius 3480 km inside a uniform rock mantle.
Energy is lost by gravitational dynamical friction, dE/dx = 4 pi G^2 M^2 rho ln(Lambda) / v^2, with ln(Lambda) = ln(R_earth v^2 / GM).
The swallowed mass uses the Hoyle-Lyttleton gas accretion rate. That is an upper bound, because solid rock does not flow in so easily.
The width of the vaporised tunnel assumes all the deposited energy goes into vaporising rock at about 1.5e7 J/kg. This is a rough upper estimate.
The seismic Mach cone uses a mean P-wave speed of 10 km/s.
The black hole is drawn hugely enlarged. Its real horizon is about 15 nanometres across, the size of a virus.
Earth is drawn as a cut-away cross-section so the path through it can be seen.

import numpy as np
import wie
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

G, c = wie.G, wie.c
M_kg = 4.3e6 * wie.M_sun
Lm = G * M_kg / c**2          # metres per geometric mass unit
Ts = G * M_kg / c**3          # seconds per geometric mass unit
AU = wie.AU

def orbit_consts(rp, ra):
    L2 = (2 / rp - 2 / ra) / ((1 - 2 / rp) / rp**2 - (1 - 2 / ra) / ra**2)
    E2 = (1 - 2 / rp) * (1 + L2 / rp**2)
    return L2, E2

def rhs_factory(L2, E):
    L = np.sqrt(L2)
    def f(phi, y):
        u = y[0]
        return [y[1], 1 / L2 - u + 3 * u * u, 1 / (L * u * u), E / (L * u * u * (1 - 2 * u))]
    return f

def periapsis_advance(rp, ra):
    L2, E2 = orbit_consts(rp, ra)
    f = rhs_factory(L2, np.sqrt(E2))
    def ev(phi, y):
        return y[1]
    ev.direction = -1
    sol = solve_ivp(f, [0, 2 * np.pi + 3.5], [1 / rp, 0, 0, 0], method="DOP853",
                    rtol=1e-12, atol=[1e-14 / rp, 1e-14 / rp, 1e-6, 1e-6], events=ev)
    ph = sol.t_events[0]
    ph = ph[ph > 1.0]
    if len(ph) == 0:
        return np.nan
    return ph[0] - 2 * np.pi

# Baseline: same geodesic code applied to Mercury around the Sun
Lsun = G * wie.M_sun / c**2
a_m = 0.387098 * AU / Lsun
e_m = 0.205630
dphi_merc = periapsis_advance(a_m * (1 - e_m), a_m * (1 + e_m))
merc_arcsec_century = dphi_merc * 206264.806 * (36525 / 87.9691)

# The what-if orbit: periapsis 8 r_s, apoapsis 20 r_s around Sgr A*
rp, ra = 16.0, 40.0
L2, E2 = orbit_consts(rp, ra)
E = np.sqrt(E2)
f = rhs_factory(L2, E)
phi = np.linspace(0, 26.0, 8000)
y = wie.solve(f, [1 / rp, 0, 0, 0], phi)
u = y[:, 0]; r = 1 / u; tau = y[:, 2]; tc = y[:, 3]
E2_end = L2 * y[-1, 1]**2 + (1 - 2 * u[-1]) * (1 + L2 * u[-1]**2)

dphi_bh = periapsis_advance(rp, ra)
dphi_deg = np.degrees(dphi_bh)
p_semi = 2 * rp * ra / (rp + ra)
weak_deg = np.degrees(6 * np.pi / p_semi)
T_rad_h = np.interp(2 * np.pi + dphi_bh, phi, tc) * Ts / 3600
a_semi = 0.5 * (rp + ra)
T_kep_h = 2 * np.pi * a_semi**1.5 * Ts / 3600

F = 300
tf = np.linspace(0, tc[-1], F)
phf = np.interp(tf, tc, phi)
rf = np.interp(phf, phi, r)
tauf = np.interp(tf, tc, tau)
k = Lm / AU
pos = np.c_[rf * np.cos(phf), rf * np.sin(phf), 0 * rf] * k
th = tf * Ts / 3600

rate = (1 - 2 / rf) / E
gam = E / np.sqrt(1 - 2 / rf)
vloc = np.sqrt(1 - 1 / gam**2)
v_peri = np.sqrt(1 - (1 - 2 / rp) / E2) * 100
rate_peri = (1 - 2 / rp) / E * 100
clock_total = tau[-1] / tc[-1] * 100
lost_h = (tc[-1] - tau[-1]) * Ts / 3600

tid_sgr = wie.tidal_acceleration(M_kg, rp * Lm, 2.0)
M10 = 10 * wie.M_sun
tid_10 = wie.tidal_acceleration(M10, rp * G * M10 / c**2, 2.0) / wie.g0

# Circular-orbit check: Schwarzschild coordinate period equals Kepler's 2 pi sqrt(r^3/GM)
rc = 20.0
L2c = rc**2 / (rc - 3)
Ec = (1 - 2 / rc) / np.sqrt(1 - 3 / rc)
yc = wie.solve(rhs_factory(L2c, Ec), [1 / rc, 0, 0, 0], np.array([0, np.pi, 2 * np.pi]))

s = wie.Scene(th, time_unit="h", length_unit="AU")
s.body("Sagittarius A*", [0, 0, 0], radius=2 * k, kind="blackhole", disk=False)
s.body("Ship", pos, radius=0.02, kind="ship", color="#ffffff")
idx = np.linspace(0, len(phi) - 1, 1500).astype(int)
s.curve("GR orbit (rosette)", np.c_[r[idx] * np.cos(phi[idx]), r[idx] * np.sin(phi[idx]), 0 * idx] * k, color="#ffaa33", width=0.8)
ang = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 400)
ecc = (ra - rp) / (ra + rp)
rn = p_semi / (1 + ecc * np.cos(ang))
s.curve("Newtonian ellipse (no shift)", np.c_[rn * np.cos(ang), rn * np.sin(ang), 0 * ang] * k, color="#4488ff", width=0.5)
s.curve("Innermost stable orbit (3 r_s)", np.c_[6 * np.cos(ang), 6 * np.sin(ang), 0 * ang] * k, color="#ff3344", width=0.5)
s.curve("Photon sphere (1.5 r_s)", np.c_[3 * np.cos(ang), 3 * np.sin(ang), 0 * ang] * k, color="#ffee88", width=0.5)

s.series("Distance from black hole", rf / 2, "r_s")
s.series("Ship clock rate vs distant clock", rate * 100, "%")
s.series("Local orbital speed", vloc * 100, "% of c")

s.number("Periapsis shift per orbit", dphi_deg, "deg", f"Weak-field formula would give {weak_deg:.0f} deg; Mercury's is {merc_arcsec_century:.1f} arcsec per century")
s.number("Orbital period seen from far away", T_rad_h, "h", f"Newton would say {T_kep_h:.2f} h for the same ellipse")
s.number("Top speed at closest approach", v_peri, "% of c", "Measured by an observer hovering there")
s.number("Ship clock rate at closest approach", rate_peri, "% of distant clock", "Gravity plus speed time dilation")
s.number("Tidal stretch on a 2 m body, Sgr A*", tid_sgr, "m/s^2", "Completely unnoticeable")
s.number("Same orbit around a 10 solar-mass black hole", tid_10, "g", "Tidal stretch on a 2 m body: lethal spaghettification")

s.caption(0, f"Your ship starts at closest approach, {rp/2:.0f} r_s ({rp*Lm/1e9:.0f} million km) from Sagittarius A*, moving at {v_peri:.1f}% of c. Your clock runs at {rate_peri:.1f}% of a distant clock.")
s.caption(th[40], f"Swinging out to {ra/2:.0f} r_s. Gravity here is so strong that the orbit does not close: each loop shifts forward by {dphi_deg:.0f} deg.")
s.caption(T_rad_h, f"Back at closest approach after {T_rad_h:.2f} h of distant time, but pointing in a new direction. Mercury's orbit shifts by only {merc_arcsec_century:.1f} arcsec per century.")
s.caption(th[200], f"You feel weightless and the tidal stretch is just {tid_sgr:.1e} m/s^2. On the same orbit around a 10 solar-mass black hole it would be {tid_10:.0f} g.")
s.caption(th[-1], f"Over the trip your clock averaged {clock_total:.1f}% of the distant rate: you aged {lost_h:.2f} h less than people far away. Inside 3 r_s no stable orbit exists.")

s.check("Baseline: same geodesic code gives Mercury's measured perihelion advance", merc_arcsec_century, 42.98, rtol=0.01)
s.check("Conserved orbital energy along the geodesic", E2_end, E2, rtol=1e-8)
s.check("Circular orbit period equals 2 pi sqrt(r^3/GM) in Schwarzschild time", yc[-1, 3], 2 * np.pi * rc**1.5, rtol=1e-7)

s.answer(f"In an orbit that comes within {rp/2:.0f} r_s of Sagittarius A*, you would feel completely weightless and reach {v_peri:.1f}% of c at closest approach, while your clock ran at only {rate_peri:.1f}% of a distant clock. The orbit does not close into an ellipse: it shifts forward by {dphi_deg:.0f} deg each loop and traces out a rosette. Around this giant black hole the tidal stretch is just {tid_sgr:.1e} m/s^2, but on the same orbit around a 10 solar-mass black hole it would be {tid_10:.0f} g and tear you apart.")
s.camera(focus="Sagittarius A*", view="top")

assumptions: The black hole is Sagittarius A* (4.3 million solar masses), not spinning (Schwarzschild).
You are a test mass in free fall on an orbit from 8 to 20 Schwarzschild radii.
Times are distant-observer (Schwarzschild coordinate) time unless stated otherwise.
There is no accretion gas, radiation or gravitational-wave loss.
The ship is drawn much larger than its real size so you can see it.
Tides are computed for a 2 m body using the Newtonian tidal formula.

import numpy as np
import wie

# ---- Sagittarius A* at full power (Eddington limit) ----
M = 4.297e6 * wie.M_sun
GM = wie.G * M
c = wie.c
r_s = 2 * GM / c**2
r_in = 6 * GM / c**2                      # ISCO, non-spinning
sigT = 6.6524587e-29                      # Thomson cross-section
L_edd = 4 * np.pi * GM * wie.m_p * c / sigT
eta = GM / (2 * r_in * c**2)              # thin-disk efficiency (Newtonian, = 1/12)
Mdot = L_edd / (eta * c**2)
Mdot_msun_yr = Mdot * wie.year / wie.M_sun
L_in_suns = L_edd / wie.L_sun
L_today = 1e29                            # W, quiet Sgr A* today (a few hundred Suns)
wake_factor = L_edd / L_today

# e-folding growth time (Salpeter) at this rate
t_grow_myr = M / Mdot / wie.year / 1e6

# a gas cloud like G2 (~3 Earth masses) would last only:
G2_minutes = 3 * wie.M_earth / Mdot / 60

# ---- What Earth sees ----
d_gc = 8178 * wie.pc
delay_yr = d_gc / wie.ly
F_earth = L_edd / (4 * np.pi * d_gc**2)
S0 = 1361.0
m_bol = -26.74 - 2.5 * np.log10(F_earth / S0)
m_visible = m_bol + 30.0                  # ~30 mag of visual dust extinction toward the centre
sun_ratio = S0 / F_earth

# ---- Thin accretion disk temperature (Shakura-Sunyaev) ----
def T_disk(r):
    return (3 * GM * Mdot / (8 * np.pi * wie.sigma_SB * r**3) * (1 - np.sqrt(r_in / r))) ** 0.25

rr = np.geomspace(r_in * 1.0000001, r_in * 1e6, 200000)
L_disk = np.trapezoid(2 * wie.sigma_SB * T_disk(rr)**4 * 2 * np.pi * rr, rr)
r_peak = rr[np.argmax(T_disk(rr))]
T_peak = T_disk(r_peak)

# ---- Star S2 on its real orbit ----
a_S2 = 0.1255 * 8178 * wie.AU
e_S2 = 0.8847
P_S2 = 2 * np.pi * np.sqrt(a_S2**3 / GM)
P_S2_yr = P_S2 / wie.year
r_apo = a_S2 * (1 + e_S2)
v_apo = np.sqrt(GM * (1 - e_S2) / (a_S2 * (1 + e_S2)))
F = 300
t_yr = np.linspace(0, 2 * P_S2_yr, F)
t = t_yr * wie.year
def orb(tt, y):
    r3 = (y[0]**2 + y[1]**2) ** 1.5
    return [y[2], y[3], -GM * y[0] / r3, -GM * y[1] / r3]
sol = wie.solve(orb, [-r_apo, 0.0, 0.0, -v_apo], t)
r_S2 = np.hypot(sol[:, 0], sol[:, 1])
E0 = 0.5 * v_apo**2 - GM / r_apo
Ef = 0.5 * (sol[-1, 2]**2 + sol[-1, 3]**2) - GM / r_S2[-1]
r_peri = a_S2 * (1 - e_S2)
F_peri = L_edd / (4 * np.pi * r_peri**2)
peri_ratio = F_peri / S0
T_S2 = 28000.0
T_day = (T_S2**4 + L_edd / (4 * np.pi * r_S2**2) / wie.sigma_SB) ** 0.25
T_day_peri = (T_S2**4 + F_peri / wie.sigma_SB) ** 0.25
i_peri = int(np.argmin(r_S2))

inc = np.radians(45)
xs = sol[:, 0] / wie.AU
ys = sol[:, 1] / wie.AU * np.cos(inc)
zs = sol[:, 1] / wie.AU * np.sin(inc)

# ---- Disk particles on Keplerian orbits ----
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
N = 2000
r_p = np.geomspace(r_in * 1.05, 200 * wie.AU, N) * (1 + 0.02 * rng.standard_normal(N))
phi0 = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, N)
Om = np.sqrt(GM / r_p**3)
ang = phi0[None, :] + Om[None, :] * t[:, None]
rA = r_p / wie.AU
zA = 0.01 * rA * rng.standard_normal(N)
pts = np.stack([rA * np.cos(ang), rA * np.sin(ang), np.broadcast_to(zA, ang.shape)], axis=-1)
Tp = T_disk(r_p)

s = wie.Scene(t_yr, time_unit="yr", length_unit="AU")
s.body("Sagittarius A*", [0, 0, 0], radius=r_s / wie.AU, kind="blackhole", disk=True)
s.body("S2 star", np.c_[xs, ys, zs], radius=10 * wie.R_sun / wie.AU, kind="star", temperature=T_day)
s.curve("S2 orbit", np.c_[xs, ys, zs], color="#88aaff", width=0.6)
s.cloud("Accretion disk gas", pts, color="#ffaa55", size=1.0, temperature=Tp)
s.camera(focus="Sagittarius A*", view="free")

s.series("S2 distance from black hole", r_S2 / wie.AU, "AU")
s.series("S2 sunlit-side temperature", T_day, "K")

s.number("Luminosity at the Eddington limit", L_in_suns / 1e9, "billion Suns", f"{L_edd:.2e} W, about {wake_factor:.0e} times brighter than today")

import numpy as np
import wie

Msun = wie.M_sun
M = 4.3e6 * Msun
GM = wie.G * M
c = wie.c
rs = 2 * GM / c**2
r0 = 10 * rs
L_body = 2.0

# exact radial geodesic from rest (cycloid in proper time)
eta = np.linspace(0, np.pi, 40001)
tau_e = np.sqrt(r0**3 / (8 * GM)) * (eta + np.sin(eta))
r_e = r0 / 2 * (1 + np.cos(eta))
tau_end = tau_e[-1]

F = 240
x = np.geomspace(1, 1e-5, F)
tau = tau_end * (1 - x)
r = np.interp(tau, tau_e, r_e)

tau_h = float(np.interp(rs, r_e[::-1], tau_e[::-1]))
dt_in = tau_end - tau_h
tau_ps = float(np.interp(1.5 * rs, r_e[::-1], tau_e[::-1]))

f = 1 - rs / r
E = np.sqrt(1 - rs / r0)
out = f > 0
v_loc = np.full(F, np.nan)
v_loc[out] = np.sqrt(np.clip(1 - f[out] / E**2, 0, 1))
ratio = np.full(F, np.nan)
ratio[out] = f[out] / (E + np.sqrt(np.clip(E**2 - f[out], 0, None)))
v_ps = np.sqrt(1 - (1 - 1 / 1.5) / E**2)

def tidal(Mk, rr):
    return 2 * wie.G * Mk * L_body / rr**3

a_t = tidal(M, r)
a_h = tidal(M, rs)
a_lim = 10 * wie.g0
r_sp = (2 * GM * L_body / a_lim) ** (1 / 3)
tau_sp = float(np.interp(r_sp, r_e[::-1], tau_e[::-1]))
t_left_sp = tau_end - tau_sp

M10 = 10 * Msun
rs10 = 2 * wie.G * M10 / c**2
a_h10_g = tidal(M10, rs10) / wie.g0
r_sp10 = (2 * wie.G * M10 * L_body / a_lim) ** (1 / 3)
tmax = np.pi * GM / c**3

inf = wie.infall(M, r0, n=300)
bh = wie.black_hole(M)
base = wie.infall(Msun, wie.AU, n=300)

tmin = tau / 60
U = 1e9
xs = r / U
pos = np.c_[xs, 0 * xs, 0 * xs]
pos[-1] = np.nan
stretch = 1 + 4 * np.tanh(a_t / a_lim)
sc = np.c_[stretch, 1 / np.sqrt(stretch), 1 / np.sqrt(stretch)]

s = wie.Scene(tmin, time_unit="min", length_unit="million km")
s.body("Sagittarius A*", [0, 0, 0], radius=rs / U, kind="blackhole", disk=True)
s.body("You", pos, radius=0.4, kind="ship", color="#ffcc66", scale=sc)
ang = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 200)
s.curve("Event horizon", np.c_[rs / U * np.cos(ang), rs / U * np.sin(ang), 0 * ang], color="#ff4444", width=0.8)
s.curve("Photon sphere", np.c_[1.5 * rs / U * np.cos(ang), 1.5 * rs / U * np.sin(ang), 0 * ang], color="#ffaa33", width=0.5)
s.curve("Your path", np.c_[np.linspace(r0, 0, 50) / U, np.zeros(50), np.zeros(50)], color="#88aaff", width=0.4)

s.series("Distance from centre", r / rs, "Schwarzschild radii")
s.series("Speed past hovering observers", v_loc, "c")
s.series("Head-to-foot tidal stretch", a_t / wie.g0, "g")
s.series("Frequency of your light reaching far observers", ratio, "x emitted")

s.number("Your time to cross the horizon", tau_h / 60, "min", "falling from rest at 10 Schwarzschild radii")
s.number("Horizon to singularity", dt_in, "s", "your own clock; no way to avoid it")
s.number("Tidal stretch at the horizon, Sgr A*", a_h, "m/s²", "over a 2 m body; you feel nothing")
s.number("Radius where stretch reaches 10 g, Sgr A*", r_sp / 1e3, "km", "spaghettification begins here, deep inside")
s.number("Tidal stretch at the horizon, 10 solar mass black hole", a_h10_g, "g", "lethal long before the horizon")
s.number("Maximum horizon-to-singularity time, Sgr A*", tmax, "s", "pi G M / c^3, best case for any trajectory")

s.caption(0, f"You start at rest 10 Schwarzschild radii ({r0/U:.0f} million km) from Sagittarius A*, whose horizon radius is {rs/U:.1f} million km.")
s.caption(tau_ps / 60, f"At the photon sphere ({1.5*rs/U:.1f} million km) light can orbit; you rush past hovering observers at {v_ps:.2f} c.")
s.caption(tau_h / 60, f"After {tau_h/60:.1f} min you cross the horizon. Tidal stretch is just {a_h:.1e} m/s², nothing to feel. Distant watchers never see this: your image freezes and redshifts to black.")
s.caption(tau_sp / 60, f"Within {r_sp/1e3:.0f} km of the centre the stretch passes 10 g: spaghettification, with {t_left_sp:.2f} s left.")
s.caption(tmin[-1], f"Classical GR: you hit the singularity {dt_in:.0f} s after the horizon (at most {tmax:.0f} s on any path). Firewalls and Planck-star bounces are competing quantum pictures. A 10 solar mass hole would tear you apart at {r_sp10/1e3:.0f} km, outside its {rs10/1e3:.1f} km horizon.")

s.check("cycloid fall time matches wie.infall geodesic", tau_end, inf["tau_to_singularity_s"], rtol=1e-3)
s.check("horizon crossing time matches wie.infall", tau_h, inf["tau_to_horizon_s"], rtol=1e-3)
s.check("pi G M/c^3 matches wie.black_hole maximum interior time", tmax, bh["max_time_horizon_to_singularity_s"], rtol=1e-6)
s.check("horizon tidal stretch matches wie.tidal_acceleration", a_h, wie.tidal_acceleration(M, rs, 2.0), rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Baseline: point Sun swallowing Earth from 1 AU in 64.57 days", base["tau_to_singularity_s"] / wie.day, 64.57, rtol=2e-3)

s.answer(f"Falling from rest at 10 Schwarzschild radii into Sagittarius A*, you would cross the event horizon after {tau_h/60:.1f} min of your own time, feeling a tidal stretch of only {a_h:.1e} m/s², because this black hole is so huge. Inside there is no way back: general relativity says you reach the centre {dt_in:.0f} s later, being spaghettified only within the last {r_sp/1e3:.0f} km. Far-away friends would never see you cross; your image would freeze, redden and fade at the horizon.")
s.camera(focus="You", view="side")

theories.name: Inside a black hole: the classical singularity
theories.summary: General relativity predicts that once inside the horizon, everything reaches the central singularity in a finite proper time. For supermassive black holes you cross the horizon unharmed and are spaghettified only near the centre. Most expect quantum gravity to modify the very centre.

theories.name: Black hole firewalls
theories.summary: To save unitarity for an old black hole, the horizon may hold a wall of high energy quanta that burns up anything falling in, instead of the smooth crossing GR predicts.

theories.summary: Collapsing matter bounces at Planck density instead of reaching a singularity; after extreme time dilation the black hole turns into a white hole and releases what fell in.

import numpy as np
import wie

G = wie.G; c = wie.c
M = 1.0e16                      # primordial black hole mass, kg
Me = wie.M_earth; R = wie.R_earth
Rc = 3.48e6; rho_c = 11000.0
Mc = 4.0 / 3.0 * np.pi * Rc**3 * rho_c
rho_m = (Me - Mc) / (4.0 / 3.0 * np.pi * (R**3 - Rc**3))

def rho_arr(r):
    return np.where(r < Rc, rho_c, np.where(r < R, rho_m, 0.0))

def Menc(r):
    if r < Rc:
        return 4.0 / 3.0 * np.pi * rho_c * r**3
    if r < R:
        return Mc + 4.0 / 3.0 * np.pi * rho_m * (r**3 - Rc**3)
    return Me

def phi(r):
    if r >= R:
        return -G * Me / r
    if r >= Rc:
        return -G * Menc(r) / r - 2 * np.pi * G * rho_m * (R**2 - r**2)
    return -G * Menc(r) / r - 2 * np.pi * G * rho_c * (Rc**2 - r**2) - 2 * np.pi * G * rho_m * (R**2 - Rc**2)

v_inf = 200e3
b = 0.25 * R
x0 = -1.6 * R
r0 = np.hypot(x0, b)
v0 = np.sqrt(v_inf**2 + 2 * G * Me / r0)
lnL = np.log(R * v_inf**2 / (G * M))

def drag(rh, v):
    return 4 * np.pi * G**2 * M**2 * rh * lnL / v**2   # dynamical friction force, N

def rhs(t, y):
    x, z, vx, vz = y
    r = np.hypot(x, z)
    ga = G * Menc(r) / r**2
    return [vx, vz, -ga * x / r, -ga * z / r]

T_end = 3.2 * R / v_inf
Nf = 24001
tf = np.linspace(0, T_end, Nf)
solf = wie.solve(rhs, [x0, b, v0, 0.0], tf)
rf = np.hypot(solf[:, 0], solf[:, 1]); vf = np.hypot(solf[:, 2], solf[:, 3])
rhf = rho_arr(rf)
Pw = drag(rhf, vf) * vf
racc_f = 2 * G * M / vf**2
dM = np.pi * racc_f**2 * rhf * vf
W_cum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(0.5 * (Pw[1:] + Pw[:-1]) * np.diff(tf))])
M_cum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(0.5 * (dM[1:] + dM[:-1]) * np.diff(tf))])
W = W_cum[-1]; M_acc = M_cum[-1]

F = 240
idx = np.linspace(0, Nf - 1, F).astype(int)
t = tf[idx]
X = solf[idx, 0]; Z = solf[idx, 1]
r_t = rf[idx]

ins = np.where(rf < R)[0]
t_in = tf[ins[0]]; t_out = tf[ins[-1]]
t_cross = t_out - t_in

vR = np.sqrt(v_inf**2 + 2 * G * Me / R)
chord = 2 * np.sqrt(R**2 - b**2)
Lc = 2 * np.sqrt(Rc**2 - b**2)
Lm = chord - Lc
W_chord = drag(rho_m, vR) * Lm + drag(rho_c, vR) * Lc
racc_R = 2 * G * M / vR**2
Macc_chord = np.pi * racc_R**2 * (rho_m * Lm + rho_c * Lc)

E0 = 0.5 * v0**2 + phi(r0)
Ef = 0.5 * vf[-1]**2 + phi(rf[-1])

kt = 4.184e12
W_kt = W / kt
dv_um = W / (M * v_inf) * 1e6

bh = wie.black_hole(M)
r_s = bh["r_s_m"]
T_H = bh["hawking_temperature_K"]
P_H = wie.hbar * c**6 / (15360 * np.pi * G**2 * M**2)

# Melt zone: rock at distance b' gets impulse kick dv = 2GM/(b' v); it melts where dv^2/2 > e_melt
e_melt = 1000.0 * 1000.0 + 4.0e5
r_melt = 2 * G * M / (vR * np.sqrt(2 * e_melt))
r_melt_cm = r_melt * 100
# fraction of drag energy deposited within the melt radius (log-distributed between b_min and R)
b_min = G * M / vR**2
frac_melt = np.log(r_melt / b_min) / np.log(R / b_min)
eta = 0.01
Mw = (np.log10(eta * W) - 4.8) / 1.5
d_ast_km = (6 * M / (np.pi * 3000.0)) ** (1 / 3) / 1e3
E_ast = 0.5 * M * (20e3)**2
ratio_ast = E_ast / W
g_surf = G * Menc(R * 0.999999) / R**2
vp = 10e3
mach_full_deg = 2 * np.degrees(np.arcsin(vp / v_inf))

km = 1e3
s = wie.Scene(t, time_unit="s", length_unit="km")
r_vis = 150.0
enlarge = r_vis * km / r_s
s.body("Tiny black hole", np.c_[X / km, 0 * X, Z / km], radius=r_vis, kind="blackhole", disk=False)
s.curve("Black hole path", np.c_[X / km, 0 * X, Z / km], color="#ff66cc", width=0.8)
ang = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 240)
s.curve("Earth surface (cutaway)", np.c_[R * np.cos(ang), 0 * ang, R * np.sin(ang)] / km, color="#3388ff", width=1.2)
s.curve("Iron core (cutaway)", np.c_[Rc * np.cos(ang), 0 * ang, Rc * np.sin(ang)] / km, color="#ffaa33", width=1.0)

rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
Ng = 1500
u = rng.normal(size=(Ng, 3)); u /= np.linalg.norm(u, axis=1)[:, None]
globe = np.broadcast_to(u * R / km, (F, Ng, 3)).copy()
s.cloud("Earth globe", globe, color="#2a6fdb", size=0.8)

Nc = 2000
ti = rng.uniform(t_in, t_out, Nc)
px = np.interp(ti, tf, solf[:, 0]); pz = np.interp(ti, tf, solf[:, 1])
ph = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, Nc)
dt = t[:, None] - ti[None, :]
rr = vp * dt
cx = np.broadcast_to(px, (F, Nc)).copy()
cy = rr * np.cos(ph)[None, :]
cz = pz[None, :] + rr * np.sin(ph)[None, :]
cone = np.stack([cx, cy, cz], axis=-1) / km
bad = (dt < 0) | (np.linalg.norm(cone, axis=-1) > R / km)
cone[bad] = np.nan
s.cloud("Seismic shock (Mach cone)", cone, color="#ffee88", size=1.0)

Nt = 600
tt = np.linspace(t_in, t_out, Nt)
tun = np.stack([np.interp(tt, tf, solf[:, 0]), 0 * tt, np.interp(tt, tf, solf[:, 1])], axis=-1) / km
tunnel = np.broadcast_to(tun, (F, Nt, 3)).copy()
tunnel[t[:, None] < tt[None, :]] = np.nan
s.cloud("Melted thread", tunnel, color="#ff6622", size=1.2, temperature=1500.0)

s.series("Energy deposited in Earth", W_cum[idx] / kt, "kt TNT")
s.series("Distance from Earth's centre", r_t / km, "km")

s.number("Schwarzschild radius", r_s, "m", "Smaller than an atom")
s.number("Time to cross Earth", t_cross, "s", "At about 200 km/s")
s.number("Energy dumped into Earth", W_kt, "kt TNT", "Dynamical friction along the whole tunnel")
s.number("Rock swallowed", M_acc, "kg", "Bondi-Hoyle accretion while passing")
s.number("Radius of melted thread", r_melt_cm, "cm", "Where the gravitational kick exceeds the melting energy")
s.number("Equivalent earthquake magnitude", Mw, "", "If 1% of the energy becomes seismic waves")

s.caption(0, f"A primordial black hole of {M:.0e} kg (the mass of a {d_ast_km:.0f} km asteroid) squeezed into a radius of {r_s:.1e} m arrives at {v_inf/1e3:.0f} km/s. Drawn {enlarge:.0e} times larger than real.")
s.caption(t_in, f"Impact. No crater: it is far smaller than an atom and slips straight into the rock, crossing Earth in {t_cross:.0f} s.")
s.caption(0.5 * (t_in + t_out), f"Its gravity yanks on the rock as it passes. Rock melts only within {r_melt_cm:.1f} cm of the track ({frac_melt*100:.0f}% of the energy); the rest leaves as a seismic Mach cone {mach_full_deg:.1f} degrees across.")
s.caption(t_out, f"It exits the far side having deposited {W_kt:.0f} kt TNT, swallowed just {M_acc:.0f} kg of rock and slowed by only {dv_um:.2f} micrometres per second.")
s.caption(T_end, f"It sails off into space. Its Hawking glow is a mere {P_H:.1f} W at {T_H:.1e} K. A rocky asteroid of the same mass would release {ratio_ast:.0e} times more energy.")

s.check("Dynamical friction energy matches straight-chord formula", W, W_chord, rtol=0.03)
s.check("Accreted mass matches Bondi-Hoyle chord estimate", M_acc, Macc_chord, rtol=0.03)
s.check("Orbital energy conserved along the path", Ef, E0, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Melt radius: impulse kinetic energy equals melting energy", 0.5 * (2 * G * M / (r_melt * vR))**2, e_melt, rtol=1e-9)
s.check("Hawking temperature matches hbar c^3/(8 pi G M k_B)", T_H, wie.hbar * c**3 / (8 * np.pi * G * M * wie.k_B), rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Baseline: two-layer Earth gives measured surface gravity 9.80 m/s^2", g_surf, 9.80, rtol=0.01)

s.answer(f"A tiny black hole of {M:.0e} kg would have a radius of only {r_s:.1e} m, smaller than an atom. It would not blast a crater; it would slip straight through the planet in about {t_cross:.0f} s. Its gravity would tug on the rock, depositing about {W_kt:.0f} kt TNT, mostly as seismic waves (roughly a magnitude {Mw:.1f} quake), and would melt rock only within {r_melt_cm:.1f} cm of its path while swallowing just {M_acc:.0f} kg. It would leave from the other side barely slowed, and Earth would be fine.")
s.camera(focus="Tiny black hole", view="side")

assumptions: The black hole is a primordial one with mass 1e16 kg, arriving at 200 km/s, a typical speed for galactic dark matter.
Earth is modelled as an iron core of 11,000 kg/m^3 and a uniform mantle, together adding up to Earth's real mass.
Energy is deposited by Chandrasekhar dynamical friction, with the Coulomb logarithm set by Earth's radius.
Swallowed rock is estimated with Bondi-Hoyle cross sections. Pressure and radiation effects on accretion are ignored.
The path is computed from Earth's gravity alone, because drag changes the speed by less than a micrometre per second.
Rock counts as melted where the black hole's gravitational kick, 2GM/(b v), delivers more than about 1.4 MJ/kg.
Assumes 1% of the deposited energy turns into seismic waves (Gutenberg-Richter energy-magnitude relation).
The black hole is drawn hugely enlarged so it can be seen. Its real radius is about 1e-11 m.
