import numpy as np
import wie

S0 = 1361.0
eps = np.radians(23.44)

def q_day(lat, dec):
    x = np.clip(-np.tan(lat) * np.tan(dec), -1.0, 1.0)
    h0 = np.arccos(x)
    Q = S0 / np.pi * (h0 * np.sin(lat) * np.sin(dec) + np.cos(lat) * np.cos(dec) * np.sin(h0))
    return np.maximum(Q, 0.0), 24.0 * h0 / np.pi

def declination(obl, lam):
    return np.arcsin(np.sin(obl) * np.sin(lam))

lam_grid = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 730, endpoint=False)
lat_grid = np.radians(np.linspace(-90, 90, 721))
L, LA = np.meshgrid(lam_grid, lat_grid, indexing="ij")
Qt, _ = q_day(LA, declination(eps, L))
Q0, _ = q_day(LA, declination(0.0, L))
w = np.cos(lat_grid)
glob_t = np.mean(np.sum(Qt * w, axis=1) / np.sum(w))
glob_0 = np.mean(np.sum(Q0 * w, axis=1) / np.sum(w))

lat_pole = np.radians(90.0); lat45 = np.radians(45.0); latL = np.radians(51.5)
pole_ann_t = np.mean(q_day(lat_pole, declination(eps, lam_grid))[0])
eq_ann_t = np.mean(q_day(0.0, declination(eps, lam_grid))[0])
eq_0 = q_day(0.0, 0.0)[0]
pole_summer_t = q_day(lat_pole, eps)[0]
q45_t = q_day(lat45, declination(eps, lam_grid))[0]
swing45 = q45_t.max() - q45_t.min()
q45_0 = q_day(lat45, 0.0)[0]
dlL_summer = q_day(latL, eps)[1]
dlL_winter = q_day(latL, -eps)[1]
dl_0 = q_day(latL, 0.0)[1]
noon45_summer = 90 - 45 + np.degrees(eps)
noon45_winter = 90 - 45 - np.degrees(eps)
noon45_0 = 45.0

# Baseline: polar-day boundary at June solstice = Arctic Circle
lats_f = np.radians(np.linspace(0, 89.999, 90000))
_, dlf = q_day(lats_f, eps)
arctic = np.degrees(lats_f[np.argmax(dlf >= 24.0 - 1e-9)])

# time grid: half a year of today, then 1.5 years untilted
tc = 182.625
tb = np.linspace(0, tc, 60, endpoint=False)
ta = np.linspace(tc, 730.5, 190)
t = np.concatenate([tb, ta])
F = len(t)
lam = 2 * np.pi * t / 365.25
obl = np.where(t < tc, eps, 0.0)
dec = declination(obl, lam)

s = wie.Scene(t, time_unit="day", length_unit="Earth radii")
spin = 2 * np.pi / 0.99727
s.body("Earth", [0, 0, 0], radius=1.0, kind="earth", spin=spin)
Dsun = wie.AU / wie.R_earth
s.body("Sun", np.c_[Dsun * np.cos(lam), Dsun * np.sin(lam), 0 * lam], radius=wie.R_sun / wie.R_earth, kind="star", temperature=5772)

n = np.c_[0 * t, np.sin(obl), np.cos(obl)]
axis = np.stack([-1.6 * n, 1.6 * n], axis=1)
s.curve("Spin axis", axis, color="#ffaa44", width=2)

phi = np.radians(np.linspace(-90, 90, 91))
QP = q_day(phi[None, :], dec[:, None])[0]
r = 1 + QP / 800.0
u = np.c_[0 * t, np.cos(obl), -np.sin(obl)]
prof = r[..., None] * (np.cos(phi)[None, :, None] * u[:, None, :] + np.sin(phi)[None, :, None] * n[:, None, :])
s.curve("Daily sunlight by latitude", prof, color="#66ccff", width=2)

q45 = q_day(lat45, dec)[0]
qpole = q_day(lat_pole, dec)[0]
dlL = q_day(latL, dec)[1]
noon45 = 90 - 45 + np.degrees(dec)

s.change(tc, "Earth's tilt drops from 23.44° to 0°")
s.series("Daily sunlight at 45°N", q45, "W/m²")
s.series("Daily sunlight at the North Pole", qpole, "W/m²")
s.series("Axial tilt", np.degrees(obl), "°")

s.on_earth("Day length in London", dlL, "h")
s.on_earth("Noon Sun height at 45°N", noon45, "°")
s.on_earth("Daily sunlight at 45°N", q45, "W/m²")

s.number("Day length everywhere with no tilt", dl_0, "h", "every latitude, every day of the year")
s.number("Seasonal swing in daily sunlight at 45°N today", swing45, "W/m²", "zero with no tilt")
s.number("Daily sunlight at 45°N with no tilt", q45_0, "W/m²", "constant all year")
s.number("Annual-mean North Pole sunlight today", pole_ann_t, "W/m²", "about 0 with no tilt")
s.number("Equator sunlight with no tilt", eq_0, "W/m²", f"vs {eq_ann_t:.0f} W/m² annual mean today")
s.number("Global mean sunlight", glob_0, "W/m²", f"unchanged: {glob_t:.1f} W/m² with tilt")

s.caption(0, f"Today: Earth is tilted 23.44°, so sunlight shifts north and south through the year. The blue outline shows daily sunlight at each latitude.")
s.caption(91.3, f"June solstice today: the North Pole gets {pole_summer_t:.0f} W/m² of daily sunlight and London has a {dlL_summer:.1f} h day.")
s.caption(tc, "The tilt vanishes at the September equinox. The spin axis now stands straight up.")
s.caption(273.9, f"December with no tilt: London still has a {dl_0:.0f} h day (today {dlL_winter:.1f} h), and 45°N keeps a steady {q45_0:.0f} W/m².")
s.caption(456.6, f"June with no tilt: no summer and no midnight sun. The poles see the Sun skimming the horizon and get almost no warmth, versus {pole_ann_t:.0f} W/m² averaged over today's year.")
s.caption(640, f"Total sunlight on Earth is unchanged at {glob_0:.1f} W/m²; it is only shared differently: the equator gets {eq_0:.0f} W/m² instead of {eq_ann_t:.0f}.")

s.earth_event(91.3, f"Today's June: London enjoys {dlL_summer:.1f} hours of daylight")
s.earth_event(tc, "Earth's axis straightens: seasons stop forever")
s.earth_event(273.9, f"No winter: London's December day lasts {dl_0:.0f} h, noon Sun stays 45° high at 45°N")
s.earth_event(456.6, "No summer either: the Arctic never sees the midnight sun again")
s.earth_event(640, "Weather becomes the same all year; only latitude decides your climate")

s.check("Baseline: polar-day edge at the June solstice equals the measured Arctic Circle", arctic, 66.563, atol=0.01)
s.check("Global mean sunlight equals S0/4 with tilt", glob_t, S0 / 4, rtol=2e-3)
s.check("Global mean sunlight equals S0/4 with no tilt", glob_0, S0 / 4, rtol=2e-3)
s.check("Annual polar sunlight matches analytic S0 sin(tilt)/pi", pole_ann_t, S0 * np.sin(eps) / np.pi, rtol=1e-3)
s.check("Untilted equator sunlight matches analytic S0/pi", eq_0, S0 / np.pi, rtol=1e-9)

s.answer(f"With no tilt there would be no seasons: every place would get {dl_0:.0f}-hour days all year, and 45°N would get a steady {q45_0:.0f} W/m² instead of swinging by {swing45:.0f} W/m² between winter and summer. The poles would sit in endless twilight.")

s.explain(f"Seasons come from obliquity, the 23.44° angle between Earth's spin axis and its orbit's axis. As Earth orbits, the solar declination swings by sin(dec) = sin(tilt) sin(orbital longitude), so each hemisphere takes turns facing the Sun. Daily-mean insolation at latitude phi is Q = (S0/pi)(h0 sin(phi) sin(dec) + cos(phi) cos(dec) sin(h0)), where the sunset hour angle comes from cos(h0) = -tan(phi) tan(dec) and S0 = {S0:.0f} W/m².\n\nToday this formula gives the North Pole {pole_summer_t:.0f} W/m² at the June solstice and {pole_ann_t:.0f} W/m² averaged over the year, while 45°N swings by {swing45:.0f} W/m² between winter and summer. London's day ranges from {dlL_winter:.1f} h to {dlL_summer:.1f} h.\n\nWith zero tilt the declination is always 0, so h0 = 90° everywhere: every latitude gets a {dl_0:.0f} h day forever, 45°N gets a constant {q45_0:.0f} W/m², the equator gets S0/pi = {eq_0:.0f} W/m² (vs {eq_ann_t:.0f} today), and the poles get essentially nothing.\n\nThe global average stays S0/4 = {glob_0:.1f} W/m², because tilt only redistributes energy. The result is a steeper equator-to-pole contrast and no seasonal cycle; the baseline check reproduces the Arctic Circle at {arctic:.2f}°N.")
s.camera(focus="Earth", view="side")

assumptions: Earth's orbit is treated as a perfect circle (real eccentricity of 0.017 ignored), so the only thing that changes sunlight through the year is tilt.
Sunlight is top-of-atmosphere daily-mean insolation; clouds, air and oceans are not modelled.
The tilt drops from 23.44° to 0° instantly at the September equinox, the moment both worlds get identical sunlight.
The Sun is treated as a point: refraction and the Sun's disk, which would give the poles a thin sliver of twilight, are ignored.
No climate model is run, so the numbers are sunlight and day length, not air temperatures.

from scipy.optimize import brentq

a0 = wie.a_moon; R = wie.R_earth

    return np.sqrt(G * Mt / a**3)

    return mu * np.sqrt(G * Mt * a)

n0 = n_of(a0)

# BEFORE: today's prograde Moon over the last 0.5 Gyr
Lpro = I * Om0 + Lorb(a0)
def Om_pro(a):
    return (Lpro - Lorb(a)) / I
def fpro(t, y):
    a = y[0]
    return [v0 * (a0 / a)**5.5 * (Om_pro(a) - n_of(a)) / (Om0 - n0)]
Tb = 0.5e9
nb = 50
tb_rev = np.linspace(0.0, -Tb, nb)
ab = wie.solve(fpro, [a0], tb_rev)[:, 0][::-1]
tb = tb_rev[::-1]
Omb = Om_pro(ab)

    return (Ltot + Lorb(a)) / I

    return [-v0 * (a0 / a)**5.5 * (Om_of(a) + n_of(a)) / (Om0 - n0)]

aa = np.interp(ta, tt, a_arr)
Oma = Om_of(aa)

T = np.concatenate([tb, ta]) / 1e9 + Tb / 1e9
Tc = Tb / 1e9
F = len(T)

import numpy as np
import wie
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp, quad

G = wie.G; M = wie.M_earth; R = wie.R_earth
rho_fe = 7870.0
rho_mean = M / (4/3*np.pi*R**3)
Rin = R * (1 - rho_mean/rho_fe) ** (1/3)
t_shell = R - Rin
q = Rin / R

def g_of_r(r, Mtot, Ri):
    r = abs(r)
    if r <= Ri:
        return 0.0
    return G*Mtot*(r**3 - Ri**3)/(R**3 - Ri**3)/r**2

def f(t, y):
    return [y[1], -np.sign(y[0])*g_of_r(y[0], M, Rin)]

g_solid = g_of_r(R, M, 0.0)
g_hollow = g_of_r(R, M, Rin)

def mk(val):
    e = lambda t, y: y[0] - val
    e.terminal = True; e.direction = -1
    return e
sol = solve_ivp(f, [0, 2e4], [R, 0.0], events=mk(0.0), rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-6, method="DOP853")
t_q = sol.t_events[0][0] if len(sol.t_events[0]) else np.nan
v_cav = abs(sol.y_events[0][0][1]) if len(sol.t_events[0]) else np.nan
sol2 = solve_ivp(f, [0, 2e4], [R, 0.0], events=mk(Rin*0.999), rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-6, method="DOP853")
v_wall = abs(sol2.y_events[0][0][1]) if len(sol2.t_events[0]) else np.nan
t_wall = sol2.t_events[0][0] if len(sol2.t_events[0]) else np.nan
T1 = 2*t_q
omega = np.sqrt(G*M/R**3)
T_uniform = np.pi/omega
dPhi, _ = quad(lambda r: g_of_r(r, M, Rin), Rin, R, epsabs=1e-6)
v_energy = np.sqrt(2*dPhi)
end = wie.solve(f, [R, 0.0], np.array([0.0, T1]))
x_far = end[-1, 0]

# Spin: angular momentum conserved, moment of inertia grows
moi_real = 0.3307          # measured Earth moment of inertia factor (input)
moi_hollow = 0.4*(1 - q**5)/(1 - q**3)
rho_sh = M/(4/3*np.pi*(R**3 - Rin**3))
I_num, _ = quad(lambda r: 8*np.pi/3*rho_sh*r**4, Rin, R)
moi_num = I_num/(M*R**2)
P_today_h = 23.9345
P_new_h = P_today_h*moi_hollow/moi_real
v_eq_today = 2*np.pi*R/(P_today_h*3600)
v_eq_new = 2*np.pi*R/(P_new_h*3600)

# Realistic thin rock crust instead of iron
rho_rock = 3300.0; tc = 100e3
M_crust = 4/3*np.pi*rho_rock*(R**3 - (R - tc)**3)
g_crust = G*M_crust/R**2
sigma = rho_rock*g_crust*R/4
strength = 200e6

# Time grid: before = one round trip through solid uniform Earth
t_c = 2*T_uniform
tb = np.linspace(0, t_c, 60, endpoint=False)
ta = np.linspace(0, 2*T1, 190)
t = np.concatenate([tb, t_c + ta])
xb = R*np.cos(omega*tb); vb = -R*omega*np.sin(omega*tb)
Y = wie.solve(f, [R, 0.0], ta)
x = np.concatenate([xb, Y[:, 0]]); v = np.concatenate([vb, Y[:, 1]])
before = t < t_c
gfelt = np.where(before, g_solid*np.abs(x)/R, np.array([g_of_r(xx, M, Rin) for xx in x]))
scale_kg = 70*gfelt/wie.g0
day = np.where(before, P_today_h, P_new_h)

tm = t/60
s = wie.Scene(tm, time_unit="min", length_unit="km")
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
N = 2200
def section(rmin):
    rr = np.sqrt(rng.uniform(rmin**2, R**2, 2*N))/1e3
    th = rng.uniform(0, 2*np.pi, 2*N)
    keep = np.abs(np.sin(th)*rr) > 150
    return np.c_[rr*np.cos(th), 0*rr, rr*np.sin(th)][keep][:N]
p_solid = section(0.0); p_shell = section(Rin)
pts = np.where(before[:, None, None], p_solid[None], p_shell[None])
s.cloud("Earth rock (cross-section)", pts, color="#8a7f74", size=2.0)
ang = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 200)
s.curve("Outer surface", np.c_[R/1e3*np.cos(ang), 0*ang, R/1e3*np.sin(ang)], color="#4fa3ff", width=2)
inner = np.c_[Rin/1e3*np.cos(ang), 0*ang, Rin/1e3*np.sin(ang)]
inner_f = np.repeat(inner[None], len(t), 0); inner_f[before] = np.nan
s.curve("Inner cavity wall", inner_f, color="#ff9a4f", width=2)
s.curve("Tunnel", np.array([[-R/1e3, 0, 0], [R/1e3, 0, 0]]), color="#555555", width=1)
s.body("Dropped ball", np.c_[x/1e3, 0*x, 0*x], radius=150, kind="rock", color="#ffffff")
s.series("Ball speed", np.abs(v)/1e3, "km/s")
s.series("Gravity felt by ball", gfelt, "m/s^2")

s.on_earth("Bathroom scale reading at the ball's depth (70 kg person)", scale_kg, "kg", today=70*g_solid/wie.g0)
s.on_earth("Rotation period of Earth", day, "hours", today=P_today_h)

s.number("Surface gravity, hollow Earth (same mass)", g_hollow, "m/s^2", "unchanged: outside, only total mass matters")
s.number("Gravity anywhere in the cavity", g_of_r(0.5*Rin, M, Rin), "m/s^2", "Newton's shell theorem")
s.number("Iron shell thickness needed", t_shell/1e3, "km", f"cavity radius {Rin/1e3:.0f} km")
s.number("Tunnel trip to far side, hollow", T1/60, "min", f"uniform solid Earth: {T_uniform/60:.1f} min")
s.number("Rotation period after hollowing", P_new_h, "h", f"today {P_today_h:.2f} h")
s.number("Crushing stress in a 100 km rock-crust shell", sigma/1e9, "GPa", "rock fails near 0.2 GPa")

s.caption(0, f"Today: solid Earth, surface gravity {g_solid:.2f} m/s^2. A ball dropped down a tunnel through a uniform Earth reaches the far side in {T_uniform/60:.1f} min and comes back")
s.change(t_c/60, "Earth becomes hollow (same mass, iron shell)")
s.caption(t_c/60 + 0.5, f"Same mass, hollow: surface gravity still {g_hollow:.2f} m/s^2, but even pure iron needs a {t_shell/1e3:.0f} km thick shell around a {Rin/1e3:.0f} km cavity")
s.caption((t_c + t_wall)/60, f"The ball leaves the shell and enters the cavity at {v_cav/1e3:.2f} km/s")
s.caption((t_c + t_q)/60, "Inside the cavity gravity is 0 m/s^2 in every direction: the ball, or you, just floats and coasts straight")
s.caption((t_c + T1)/60, f"It reaches the far side in {T1/60:.1f} min. Meanwhile mass moved outward, so Earth's spin slows: a day lasts {P_new_h:.1f} h instead of {P_today_h:.2f} h, and the equator moves at {v_eq_new:.0f} m/s instead of {v_eq_today:.0f} m/s")
s.caption((t_c + 1.5*T1)/60, f"A real thin crust can't do this: a 100 km rock shell has only {g_crust:.3f} m/s^2 gravity yet carries {sigma/1e9:.1f} GPa of stress, about {sigma/strength:.0f}x what rock can take, so it collapses")

s.earth_event(t_c/60, f"Earth's insides vanish, yet the ground still pulls you with {g_hollow:.2f} m/s^2")
s.earth_event(t_c/60 + 1, f"Earth's spin slows: each day now lasts {P_new_h:.1f} hours")
s.earth_event((t_c + t_q)/60, "Anyone down in the cavity weighs 0 kg and floats freely")
s.earth_event((t_c + 1.5*T1)/60, f"A thin rock crust would be crushed by {sigma/1e9:.1f} GPa and cave in")

s.check("Baseline: solid Earth surface gravity vs measured 9.81 m/s^2", g_solid, 9.81, rtol=0.01)
s.check("Cavity speed matches energy conservation", v_cav, v_energy, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Speed constant across cavity (zero gravity inside shell)", v_wall, v_cav, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Ball turns around at the far surface (energy conserved)", x_far, -R, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Shell moment of inertia: numeric integral vs analytic formula", moi_num, moi_hollow, rtol=1e-8)

s.answer(f"With the same mass, a hollow Earth still pulls you down with {g_hollow:.2f} m/s^2 at the surface, but inside the cavity gravity is 0, so you'd float. Earth's spin would slow, making the day {P_new_h:.1f} h, and even solid iron would need a {t_shell/1e3:.0f} km thick shell; a thin rock crust would collapse.")

s.explain(f"Newton's shell theorem says a spherical shell pulls on outside objects as if all its mass sat at the centre, and exerts zero net force anywhere inside. So with Earth's mass kept, surface gravity stays g = G M / R^2 = {g_hollow:.2f} m/s^2, while every point in the cavity has g = 0.\n\nTo hold Earth's mass of {M:.3e} kg with iron (density {rho_fe:.0f} kg/m^3), the shell must satisfy M = (4/3) pi rho (R^3 - Rin^3), giving Rin = {Rin/1e3:.0f} km and a thickness of {t_shell/1e3:.0f} km. Inside the shell gravity is g(r) = G M (r^3 - Rin^3) / ((R^3 - Rin^3) r^2). Integrating a ball dropped down a tunnel gives {v_cav/1e3:.2f} km/s at the cavity wall, constant across the cavity, and a trip of {T1/60:.1f} min versus {T_uniform/60:.1f} min for a uniform solid Earth.\n\nConservation of angular momentum (L = I omega) sets the new spin. The moment of inertia factor rises from the measured {moi_real} to 0.4(1 - q^5)/(1 - q^3) = {moi_hollow:.3f} with q = Rin/R = {q:.3f}, so the rotation period stretches from {P_today_h:.2f} h to {P_new_h:.1f} h.\n\nA thin rock crust fails: a 100 km shell has surface gravity {g_crust:.3f} m/s^2 but membrane stress sigma = rho g R / 4 = {sigma/1e9:.1f} GPa, far above rock's ~0.2 GPa compressive strength.")
s.camera(focus="Dropped ball", view="side")

assumptions: Earth keeps its present mass and radius; the hollow version is a uniform pure-iron shell around an empty spherical cavity.
The 'today' tunnel drop uses a uniform-density Earth; the real denser core would make it about 38 min.
The tunnel is airless and frictionless, and Earth's rotation is ignored for the ball's motion.
The day-length change assumes the interior is rearranged instantly with angular momentum conserved, using today's measured moment of inertia factor 0.3307.
Where the guesswork starts: no real material could build or hold up such a shell, so its strength is only checked roughly for a 100 km rock crust using thin-shell membrane stress.

assumptions: Planets start on circular, coplanar orbits at their real average distances, spread out at different angles.
The Moon, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets are left out; their gravity barely changes the planets' orbits.
Jupiter vanishes instantly, and its gravity disappears everywhere at the same moment.

r0 = wie.AU
rc = wie.R_sun + wie.R_earth
red = wie.M_sun * wie.M_earth / (wie.M_sun + wie.M_earth)

def f(t, y):
    return [y[1], -mu / y[0]**2]
def hit(t, y):
    return y[0] - rc
hit.terminal = True
hit.direction = -1
sol = solve_ivp(f, [0, 200 * wie.day], [r0, 0.0], method="DOP853", rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-3,
                events=hit, dense_output=True)
if len(sol.t_events[0]) > 0:
    t_c = sol.t_events[0][0]
    v_imp = abs(sol.y_events[0][0][1])
else:
    t_c = sol.t[-1]
    v_imp = abs(sol.y[1, -1])

def t_of_r(r):
    x = r / r0
    return np.sqrt(r0**3 / (2 * mu)) * (np.sqrt(x * (1 - x)) + np.arccos(np.sqrt(x)))

t_an = t_of_r(rc)
v_an = np.sqrt(2 * mu * (1 / rc - 1 / r0))
P_year = 2 * np.pi * np.sqrt(r0**3 / mu)
v_orb = np.sqrt(mu / r0)
omega = 2 * np.pi / P_year

A = 0.3

r_melt = r_for_surface(1500.0)
t_venus = t_of_r(0.723 * wie.AU)
t_merc = t_of_r(0.387 * wie.AU)
t_boil = t_of_r(r_boil)
t_melt = t_of_r(r_melt)

rho_s = wie.M_sun / (4 / 3 * np.pi * wie.R_sun**3)
rho_e = wie.M_earth / (4 / 3 * np.pi * wie.R_earth**3)

nb = len(t_before)
nf = len(t_fall)
Mkm = 1e9

earth = np.full((F, 3), np.nan)
phi = omega * (t_before - Tb)
earth[:nb, 0] = r0 * np.cos(phi) / Mkm
earth[:nb, 1] = r0 * np.sin(phi) / Mkm
earth[:nb, 2] = 0.0
earth[nb:nb + nf, 0] = r_fall / Mkm
earth[nb:nb + nf, 1] = 0.0
earth[nb:nb + nf, 2] = 0.0

r_all[nb:nb + nf] = r_fall

N = 2000
dirs = rng.normal(size=(N, 3)); dirs /= np.linalg.norm(dirs, axis=1)[:, None]

import numpy as np
import wie

S0 = 1361.0
eps_now = np.radians(23.44)
eps_new = np.radians(98.0)

lat_L = 51.5

def decl(lam, eps):
    return np.arcsin(np.sin(eps) * np.sin(lam))

def Q(lat_deg, dec):
    phi = np.radians(lat_deg)
    h0 = np.arccos(np.clip(-np.tan(phi) * np.tan(dec), -1.0, 1.0))
    return S0 / np.pi * (h0 * np.sin(phi) * np.sin(dec) + np.cos(phi) * np.cos(dec) * np.sin(h0))

def daylight_h(lat_deg, dec):
    phi = np.radians(lat_deg)
    h0 = np.arccos(np.clip(-np.tan(phi) * np.tan(dec), -1.0, 1.0))
    return h0 / np.pi * 24.0

def noon_alt(lat_deg, dec):
    return 90.0 - np.abs(lat_deg - np.degrees(dec))

def pole_Q(dec):
    return S0 * np.clip(np.sin(dec), 0, None)

eq_ann_new = Q(0.0, dw).mean()

pole_summer_now = S0 * np.sin(eps_now)

s.earth_event(tb, "Earth's axis tips over onto its side")

s.earth_event(tb + YEAR_D * 0.25, f"Sun almost overhead at the North Pole, {pole_summer_new:.0f} W/m² nonstop")

s.check("Baseline: today's Arctic Circle latitude (66°33.8')", arctic_now, 66.563, rtol=1e-3)
s.check("Global mean sunlight is S0/4 regardless of tilt", glob_new, S0 / 4, rtol=2e-3)

s.explain(f"""This model uses the geometry of sunlight on a rotating planet in a circular orbit. The Sun's declination follows sin(delta) = sin(eps) sin(lambda), where eps is the obliquity and lambda the Sun's orbital longitude. Daily mean top-of-atmosphere insolation is Q = (S0/pi)(h0 sin(phi) sin(delta) + cos(phi) cos(delta) sin(h0)), with sunset hour angle cos(h0) = -tan(phi) tan(delta) and S0 = {S0:.0f} W/m².

At the June solstice the North Pole receives S0 sin(eps) = {pole_summer_new:.0f} W/m² continuously, versus {pole_summer_now:.0f} W/m² today. Averaged over the year the pole gets S0 sin(eps)/pi = {pole_ann_new:.0f} W/m² (today {pole_ann_now:.0f}), while the equator drops to {eq_ann_new:.0f} W/m² (today {eq_ann_now:.0f}): the insolation gradient between equator and poles reverses.

At London (51.5°N) the year splits into {mid_L_new:.0f} days of midnight sun and {dark_L_new:.0f} days of polar night. The spin counts as retrograde relative to the orbital plane, but the ground still turns toward the east, so the Sun still rises in the east.

The global mean insolation stays S0/4 = {S0/4:.0f} W/m², because obliquity only redistributes sunlight. Atmosphere, oceans and heat transport are not modelled, so these are sunlight inputs, not temperatures.""")
s.camera(focus="Earth", view="free")

Tilt set to 98°, close to Uranus's 97.77°.
Sunlight is computed at the top of the atmosphere; clouds, oceans and winds are not modelled.
The tilt changes instantly at the March equinox; nothing physical could tip Earth this way.
Day length and orbit stay as they are today; geographic north is kept as today's North Pole.
Sunrise is taken as the geometric centre of the Sun crossing the horizon, with no atmospheric refraction.

import numpy as np
import wie
from scipy.special import ellipk

G = wie.G; M = wie.M_earth; RE = wie.R_earth
V = 4/3*np.pi*RE**3
k = 2.0
a = (V/(2*np.pi**2*k))**(1/3)
R = k*a

def potential(rr, zz, mm, rho, z, excl):
    d2 = (rho[:, None]+rr[None, :])**2 + (z[:, None]-zz[None, :])**2
    mk = np.minimum(4*rr[None, :]*rho[:, None]/d2, 1-1e-14)
    dist = np.sqrt((rho[:, None]-rr[None, :])**2 + (z[:, None]-zz[None, :])**2)
    term = G*mm[None, :]*2/np.pi*ellipk(mk)/np.sqrt(d2)
    term = np.where(dist < excl, 0.0, term)
    return -term.sum(axis=1)

def gfield(src, rho, z, h, excl):
    rr, zz, mm = src
    gr = -(potential(rr, zz, mm, rho+h, z, excl)-potential(rr, zz, mm, rho-h, z, excl))/(2*h)
    gz = -(potential(rr, zz, mm, rho, z+h, excl)-potential(rr, zz, mm, rho, z-h, excl))/(2*h)
    return gr, gz

def torus_rings(n):
    u = (np.arange(n)+0.5)/n*2-1
    U, W = np.meshgrid(u, u)
    ins = U**2+W**2 < 1
    rr = R+a*U[ins]; zz = a*W[ins]
    mm = M*rr/rr.sum()
    return rr, zz, mm, 2*a/n

def spin_rate(n):
    rr, zz, mm, cell = torus_rings(n)
    gr, gz = gfield((rr, zz, mm), rr, zz, 0.02*cell, 0.3*cell)
    return np.sqrt(np.sum(mm*(-gr))/np.sum(mm*rr))

w = spin_rate(36)
w_coarse = spin_rate(26)
T_day_h = 2*np.pi/w/3600

rr, zz, mm, cell = torus_rings(60)
th = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 73)[:-1]
rs = R+a*np.cos(th); zs = a*np.sin(th)
gr, gz = gfield((rr, zz, mm), rs, zs, 0.05*cell, 0.3*cell)
ger = gr + w**2*rs
gn = -(ger*np.cos(th)+gz*np.sin(th))
gt = -ger*np.sin(th)+gz*np.cos(th)
gn0 = -(gr*np.cos(th)+gz*np.sin(th))
slope = np.degrees(np.arctan2(np.abs(gt), gn))

g_out, g_top, g_in = gn[i_out], gn[i_top], gn[i_in]
g_out_nospin = gn0[i_out]; g_in_nospin = gn0[i_in]

v_ground = w*(R+a)

hole_km = 2*(R-a)/1e3
outer_km = (R+a)/1e3
tube_km = 2*a/1e3

# Baseline: same ring-summation code applied to today's spherical Earth
nb = 60
ur = (np.arange(nb)+0.5)/nb*RE
uz = (np.arange(2*nb)+0.5)/(2*nb)*2*RE-RE

insb = Rg**2+Zg**2 < RE**2
srr = Rg[insb]; szz = Zg[insb]; smm = M*srr/srr.sum()
cb = RE/nb
_, gz_pole = gfield((srr, szz, smm), np.array([1e-3*cb]), np.array([RE]), 0.05*cb, 0.3*cb)

w_earth = 2*np.pi/23.934
ang = np.where(before, w_earth*t, w_earth*T0 + w*3600*(t-T0))

rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
Np = 2400

rho_p = (R+a*np.cos(tq))/RE; z_p = a*np.sin(tq)/RE

ZZ = np.where(before[:, None], z_s[None, :], z_p[None, :])

turns = np.where(before, t/23.934, T0/23.934 + (t-T0)/T_day_h)
s.series("Length of day", day, "h")
s.series("Turns completed", turns, "turns")

w70_out = 70*g_out/wie.g0; w70_in = 70*g_in/wie.g0; w70_top = 70*g_top/wie.g0
w70_today = 70*9.80/wie.g0
s.on_earth("Length of day", day, "h", today=23.934)
s.on_earth("Scale reading for 70 kg at the outer equator", np.where(before, w70_today, w70_out), "kg", today=70.0)
s.on_earth("Scale reading for 70 kg at the inner equator", np.where(before, w70_today, w70_in), "kg", today=70.0)

s.number("Length of a day", T_day_h, "h", "spin needed to stop the ring collapsing")
s.number("Scale reading for 70 kg at the outer equator", w70_out, "kg", f"felt gravity {g_out:.2f} m/s², {g_out_nospin:.2f} without spin")
s.number("Scale reading for 70 kg at the top of the ring", w70_top, "kg", f"felt gravity {g_top:.2f} m/s²")
s.number("Scale reading for 70 kg at the inner equator", w70_in, "kg", f"felt gravity {g_in:.2f} m/s²; spin pushes you down here")
s.number("Ground speed at the outer equator", v_ground, "m/s", f"today's equator moves at {v_earth_eq:.0f} m/s")
s.number("Width of the hole", hole_km, "km", f"outer radius {outer_km:.0f} km, tube {tube_km:.0f} km thick")

s.caption(0, "Today: a round Earth, 12,742 km across, turning once every 23.93 hours, felt gravity about 9.8 m/s².")
s.change(T0, "Earth is reshaped into a donut with the same mass and volume")
s.caption(T0+0.1, f"The donut is {2*outer_km:,.0f} km across with a {hole_km:,.0f} km hole and a tube {tube_km:,.0f} km thick.")
s.caption(T0+0.3*T_day_h, f"Gravity pulls the ring toward its centre line and inward; only a {T_day_h:.1f} h day keeps the hole open.")
s.caption(T0+0.8*T_day_h, f"The outer equator races at {v_ground:.0f} m/s (today {v_earth_eq:.0f} m/s), roughly a rifle bullet's speed.")
s.caption(T0+1.3*T_day_h, f"70 kg reads {w70_out:.0f} kg on the outer equator, {w70_top:.0f} kg on top and {w70_in:.0f} kg on the inner equator.")
s.caption(T0+1.8*T_day_h, f"Felt gravity tilts up to {slope_max:.0f}° from straight down on a round tube, so oceans would flow and reshape it; thick rings like this tend to clump into blobs.")

s.earth_event(T0, f"Earth becomes a ring {2*outer_km:,.0f} km wide with a {hole_km:,.0f} km hole")
s.earth_event(T0+0.5*T_day_h, f"Days shrink from 24 h to {T_day_h:.1f} h")
s.earth_event(T0+1.0*T_day_h, f"A 70 kg person weighs {w70_in:.0f} kg on the inner shore, {w70_out:.0f} kg on the outer")
s.earth_event(T0+1.5*T_day_h, "From the inner shore, the far side of the ring arches overhead across the sky")

s.check("Baseline: same ring-sum code gives today's surface gravity GM/R^2 ≈ 9.82 m/s²", g_sphere_pole, 9.82, rtol=1e-2)
s.check("Far field of the donut approaches a point mass GM/r^2", -gzf[0], G*M/zfar**2, rtol=3e-3)

d0 = 1.0 * AU
d1 = 0.387098 * AU

RE = wie.R_earth
sig = wie.sigma_SB
gE = wie.g0

def flux(d):
    return wie.L_sun / (4 * np.pi * d**2)

def t_eq(d, albedo=A):
    return (flux(d) * (1 - albedo) / (4 * sig)) ** 0.25

def rhs(tt, y):
    r3 = (y[0]**2 + y[1]**2) ** 1.5
    return [y[2], y[3], -mu*y[0]/r3, -mu*y[1]/r3]

def orbit(d, t, phi=0.0):
    v = np.sqrt(mu / d)
    return wie.solve(rhs, [d*np.cos(phi), d*np.sin(phi), -v*np.sin(phi), v*np.cos(phi)], t)

def period_numeric(d):
    Pg = 2*np.pi*np.sqrt(d**3/mu)
    tt = np.linspace(0, 1.2*Pg, 4001)
    sol = orbit(d, tt)
    ang = np.unwrap(np.arctan2(sol[:, 1], sol[:, 0]))
    return np.interp(2*np.pi, ang, tt)

import numpy as np
import wie
from scipy.optimize import brentq

GM = wie.G * wie.M_earth
M = wie.M_earth
R_eq = 6378137.0
R_mean = 6371000.0
T_sid = 86164.1
w0 = 2*np.pi/T_sid
k = 10.0
w = k*w0
T_new = T_sid/k
C_norm = 0.3307
V0 = 4/3*np.pi*R_mean**3
f_meas = 1/298.257

def g_eff_sphere(omega, a):
    return GM/a**2 - omega**2*a

def flattening_darwin_radau(omega, a):
    m = omega**2*a**3/GM
    return 2.5*m/(1+6.25*(1-1.5*C_norm)**2)

# ---------- Model A (lower bound): Roche, all mass at the centre ----------
th = np.linspace(0, np.pi, 181)
def roche_surface(omega, rp):
    q = omega**2*rp**3/GM
    xs = np.ones_like(th)
    for i in range(len(th)):
        s2 = np.sin(th[i])**2
        if s2 < 1e-12:
            continue
        xmax = (1/(q*s2))**(1/3)
        fn = lambda x: 1/x + 0.5*q*s2*x**2 - 1
        xs[i] = brentq(fn, 1.0, xmax, xtol=1e-14)
    return xs*rp
def roche_volume(omega, rp):
    r = roche_surface(omega, rp)
    return 2*np.pi/3*np.trapezoid(r**3*np.sin(th), th)
def roche_shape(omega):
    rp_max = (8/27*GM/omega**2)**(1/3)*(1-1e-9)
    hi = min(rp_max, R_mean)
    rp = brentq(lambda r: roche_volume(omega, r) - V0, 0.5*R_mean, hi, xtol=1e-3)
    return rp, roche_surface(omega, rp)[90]

# ---------- Model B: dense point core + uniform envelope, spheroidal figure ----------
# potential of a homogeneous oblate spheroid (Chandrasekhar index symbols) + point core + centrifugal
egrid = np.linspace(0.01, 0.995, 4000)
def spheroid_terms(e):
    s1 = np.sqrt(1 - e**2)
    ase = np.arcsin(e)
    A1 = s1*ase/e**3 - (1 - e**2)/e**2
    A3 = 2/e**2 - 2*s1*ase/e**3
    I0 = 2*s1*ase/e
    a = (V0*3/(4*np.pi)/s1)**(1/3)
    c = a*s1
    return A1, A3, I0, a, c
A1g, A3g, I0g, ag, cg = spheroid_terms(egrid)

def figure(omega, mu):
    rho = (1 - mu)*M/V0
    Mc = mu*M
    phi_eq = -np.pi*wie.G*rho*ag**2*(I0g - A1g) - wie.G*Mc/ag - 0.5*omega**2*ag**2
    phi_po = -np.pi*wie.G*rho*(I0g*ag**2 - A3g*cg**2) - wie.G*Mc/cg
    D = phi_eq - phi_po
    idx = np.where(np.sign(D[:-1]) != np.sign(D[1:]))[0]
    if len(idx) == 0:
        return None
    j = idx[0]
    fn = lambda e: (lambda A1, A3, I0, a, c: -np.pi*wie.G*rho*a**2*(I0 - A1) - wie.G*Mc/a - 0.5*omega**2*a**2
                    + np.pi*wie.G*rho*(I0*a**2 - A3*c**2) + wie.G*Mc/c)(*spheroid_terms(e))
    e = brentq(fn, egrid[j], egrid[j+1], xtol=1e-13)
    A1, A3, I0, a, c = spheroid_terms(e)
    g_eq = 2*np.pi*wie.G*rho*A1*a + wie.G*Mc/a**2 - omega**2*a
    return a, c, 1 - c/a, g_eq

# calibrate the core fraction so today's spin gives the measured flattening
mu = brentq(lambda u: figure(w0, u)[2] - f_meas, 0.0, 0.99, xtol=1e-12)
C_model = 0.4*(1 - mu)
resB = figure(w, mu)
have_B = resB is not None

v_today = w0*R_eq
v_new = w*R_eq
g_today = g_eff_sphere(w0, R_eq)
g_inst = g_eff_sphere(w, R_eq)
frac_inst = w/np.sqrt(GM/R_eq**3)
cent_frac = w**2*R_eq/(GM/R_eq**2)
dE = 0.5*C_norm*M*R_eq**2*(w**2 - w0**2)
f_DR_today = flattening_darwin_radau(w0, R_eq)
f_DR_new = flattening_darwin_radau(w, R_eq)

rpA, aA = roche_shape(w)
fA = 1 - rpA/aA
gA = g_eff_sphere(w, aA)
rp0, a0 = roche_shape(w0)
f_roche_today = 1 - rp0/a0
m_today = w0**2*rp0**3/GM

if have_B:
    aB, cB, fB, gB = resB
    fracB = np.sqrt(w**2*aB/(gB + w**2*aB))
else:
    aB, cB, fB, gB = aA, rpA, fA, gA
    fracB = 1.0
a_show, c_show, g_show = aB, cB, gB

# ocean response before rock deforms
dPhi = 0.5*(w**2 - w0**2)*R_eq**2
h_ocean = dPhi/g_today

scale_today_kg = 70*g_today/wie.g0
scale_inst_kg = 70*g_inst/wie.g0
scale_rel_kg = 70*g_show/wie.g0

tc = 6.0
t1 = np.linspace(0, tc, 50)
t2 = tc + np.linspace(0, 24, 201)[1:]
hrs = np.concatenate([t1, t2])
F = len(hrs)
after = hrs > tc
tau = np.where(after, hrs - tc, 0.0)
relax = 1 - np.exp(-tau/4.0)
c_today = R_eq*(1 - f_meas)
a_t = R_eq + (a_show - R_eq)*relax
c_t = c_today + (c_show - c_today)*relax
omega_t = np.where(after, w, w0)
g_t = np.where(after, g_inst + (g_show - g_inst)*relax, g_today)

s = wie.Scene(hrs, time_unit="h", length_unit="Earth radii")
pb = np.zeros((F, 3)); pb[after] = np.nan
pa = np.zeros((F, 3)); pa[~after] = np.nan
s.body("Earth (today)", pb, radius=1.0, kind="earth", scale=[R_eq/R_mean, R_eq/R_mean, c_today/R_mean], spin=w0*3600)
s.body("Earth", pa, radius=1.0, kind="earth", scale=np.c_[a_t/R_mean, a_t/R_mean, c_t/R_mean], spin=w*3600)
ang = np.where(after, w0*tc*3600 + w*(hrs - tc)*3600, w0*hrs*3600)
rm = a_t/R_mean*1.03
s.body("Equator marker", np.c_[rm*np.cos(ang), rm*np.sin(ang), 0*hrs], radius=0.04, kind="particle", color="#ff5533")
ang0 = w0*hrs*3600
s.body("Today's pace marker", np.c_[rm*np.cos(ang0), rm*np.sin(ang0), 0*hrs + 0.08], radius=0.04, kind="particle", color="#33aaff")
s.change(tc, "Earth suddenly spins 10 times faster")

s.series("Turns completed", ang/(2*np.pi), "turns")
s.series("Felt gravity at equator", g_t, "m/s^2")
s.series("Equatorial radius", a_t/1e3, "km")

s.on_earth("Length of a day", np.where(after, T_new, T_sid)/3600, "h", today=23.93)
s.on_earth("Bathroom scale reading for a 70 kg person at the equator", 70*g_t/wie.g0, "kg", today=scale_today_kg)
s.on_earth("Ground speed at the equator", omega_t*R_eq*3.6, "km/h", today=1674)

jet = 900/3.6
bullet = 900.0
s.number("New day length", T_new/3600, "h", "today 23.93 h")
s.number("Equator ground speed", v_new*3.6, "km/h", f"today {v_today*3.6:.0f} km/h")
s.number("Scale reading for 70 kg at equator, right after spin-up", scale_inst_kg, "kg", f"today {scale_today_kg:.1f} kg")
s.number("Equatorial radius, calibrated core-envelope model", aB/1e3, "km", f"poles {cB/1e3:.0f} km; least-deformable Roche bound {aA/1e3:.0f} km")
s.number("Flattening, calibrated model", fB, "", f"range {fA:.2f} (Roche) to Darwin-Radau extrapolation {f_DR_new:.2f}; today 0.0034")
s.number("Extra rotational energy", dE, "J", "energy needed to spin Earth up")

s.caption(0, f"Today: Earth turns once every 23.93 h and the equator moves at {v_today*3.6:.0f} km/h.")
s.caption(tc, f"Spin-up: the day shrinks to {T_new/3600:.2f} h. The equator races at {v_new*3.6:.0f} km/h, {v_new/jet:.0f} times a jet airliner and {v_new/bullet:.1f} times a rifle bullet.")
s.caption(tc + 1, f"Spin now cancels {cent_frac*100:.0f}% of gravity at the equator: felt gravity drops from {g_today:.2f} to {g_inst:.2f} m/s^2.")
s.caption(tc + 4, f"The sea surface wants to tilt by about {h_ocean/1e3:.0f} km from pole to equator, far more than the ocean is deep, so the oceans drain from the poles toward the equator.")
if have_B:
    s.caption(tc + 10, f"Rock flows too. A dense-core model that matches today's flattening gives an equator at {aB/1e3:.0f} km and poles at {cB/1e3:.0f} km (flattening {fB:.2f}). The stiffest possible case still reaches {aA/1e3:.0f} km.")
    s.caption(tc + 18, f"On the bulge, felt gravity at the equator is {gB:.2f} m/s^2 (a 70 kg person weighs {scale_rel_kg:.0f} kg), and the spin is {fracB:.2f} of the rate that would fling rock into orbit. Earth survives, though it may end up as a three-axis (triaxial) shape.")
else:
    s.caption(tc + 10, f"No spheroidal equilibrium exists in the core-envelope model: the equator sheds mass. The stiffest-case bound pushes it out to at least {aA/1e3:.0f} km.")

s.earth_event(tc, f"Sunrise to sunrise now takes just {T_new/3600:.1f} hours")
s.earth_event(tc + 0.5, f"A 70 kg person at the equator weighs {scale_inst_kg:.0f} kg on a scale")
s.earth_event(tc + 4, "Oceans pour off the poles toward a huge equatorial bulge")
s.earth_event(tc + 18, f"The equator swells out to {aB/1e3:.0f} km from the centre; scales read {scale_rel_kg:.0f} kg")

s.check("Baseline: Darwin-Radau flattening today matches measured 1/298.257", f_DR_today, 1/298.257, rtol=0.02)
s.check("Baseline: today's equatorial felt gravity matches measured 9.780 m/s^2", g_today, 9.7803, rtol=0.005)
s.check("Baseline: calibrated model moment of inertia close to measured C/MR^2 0.3307", C_model, 0.3307, rtol=0.15)
s.check("Roche model in slow-spin limit gives f = m/2", f_roche_today, m_today/2, rtol=0.03)
mm = w0**2*R_mean**3/GM
s.check("Uniform-density limit of figure model gives Maclaurin f = 5m/4", figure(w0, 0.0)[2], 1.25*mm, rtol=0.03)
s.check("Relaxed Roche shape keeps Earth's volume", roche_volume(w, rpA), V0, rtol=1e-4)

if have_B:
    s.answer(f"A day would last only {T_new/3600:.2f} hours and the equator would race at {v_new*3.6:.0f} km/h. Right away a 70 kg person at the equator would weigh {scale_inst_kg:.0f} kg, and Earth would squash until its equator sat about {aB/1e3:.0f} km from the centre (at least {aA/1e3:.0f} km).")
else:
    s.answer(f"A day would last only {T_new/3600:.2f} hours and the equator would race at {v_new*3.6:.0f} km/h. A 70 kg person there would weigh {scale_inst_kg:.0f} kg, and the bulging equator, at least {aA/1e3:.0f} km out, would begin shedding rock.")

The extra rotational kinetic energy is 0.5 I (w^2 - w0^2) = {dE:.2e} J.\n\nIn the rotating frame the felt gravity is g_eff = G M / R^2 - w^2 R. The spin reaches {fracB:.2f} of the breakup rate.")
s.camera(focus="Earth", view="side")

import numpy as np
import wie
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
from scipy.optimize import brentq

rho0 = 19300.0
K0 = 167e9
Kp = 6.0
R = wie.R_earth

def rho_of_P(P):
    return rho0*np.maximum(1 + Kp*P/K0, 1e-9)**(1/Kp)

def structure(Pc, dense=False):
    r0 = 1.0
    rc = rho_of_P(Pc)
    def f(r, y):
        m, P = y
        rho = rho_of_P(P)
        return [4*np.pi*r**2*rho, -wie.G*m*rho/r**2]
    def surf(r, y):
        return y[1]
    surf.terminal = True
    surf.direction = -1
    sol = solve_ivp(f, [r0, 1e8], [4/3*np.pi*r0**3*rc, Pc], events=surf,
                    rtol=1e-10, atol=[1e3, 1e-3], method="DOP853", dense_output=dense)
    if len(sol.t_events[0]) > 0:
        return sol.t_events[0][0], sol.y_events[0][0][0], sol
    return sol.t[-1], sol.y[0, -1], sol

Pc = brentq(lambda p: structure(p)[0] - R, 1e11, 2e13, xtol=1e3)
Rg, M_gold, solg = structure(Pc, dense=True)
ratio = M_gold/wie.M_earth
rho_c = rho_of_P(Pc)
rho_mean = M_gold/(4/3*np.pi*R**3)
P_center_GPa = Pc/1e9

rr = np.linspace(1.0, Rg, 4000)
M_trap = np.trapezoid(4*np.pi*rr**2*rho_of_P(solg.sol(rr)[1]), rr)
Pc_small = 1e6
R_small, M_small, sm = structure(Pc_small)
R_small_exp = np.sqrt(Pc_small/(2*np.pi/3*wie.G*rho0**2))

def surface_g(M, r):
    return wie.G*M/r**2
g_real = surface_g(wie.M_earth, R)
g_gold = surface_g(M_gold, R)
v_esc_real = np.sqrt(2*wie.G*wie.M_earth/R)/1e3
v_esc = np.sqrt(2*wie.G*M_gold/R)/1e3
weight70 = 70*g_gold/g_real
p_bar = 1.013*g_gold/g_real

mu_old = wie.G*(wie.M_earth + wie.M_moon)
mu_new = wie.G*(M_gold + wie.M_moon)
a0 = wie.a_moon
v0 = np.sqrt(mu_old/a0)
P_real_d = 2*np.pi*np.sqrt(a0**3/mu_old)/wie.day
a_new = 1/(2/a0 - v0**2/mu_new)
e_new = a0/a_new - 1
r_peri = a_new*(1 - e_new)
P_new_d = 2*np.pi*np.sqrt(a_new**3/mu_new)/wie.day
rho_moon = wie.M_moon/(4/3*np.pi*wie.R_moon**3)
roche_fluid = 2.44*R*(rho_mean/rho_moon)**(1/3)
roche_rigid = 1.26*R*(rho_mean/rho_moon)**(1/3)
inside_fluid = r_peri < roche_fluid
inside_rigid = r_peri < roche_rigid
if inside_rigid:
    roche_txt = f"inside even the {roche_rigid/1e3:.0f} km rigid-body Roche limit: the Moon would be torn apart"
elif inside_fluid:
    roche_txt = f"inside the {roche_fluid/1e3:.0f} km fluid Roche limit but outside the {roche_rigid/1e3:.0f} km rigid limit: solid rock probably holds, under heavy tidal stress"
else:
    roche_txt = f"outside the {roche_fluid/1e3:.0f} km fluid Roche limit"

tc_d = 6.0
t1 = np.linspace(0, tc_d, 60)
t2 = np.linspace(tc_d, tc_d + 2.5*P_new_d, 201)
td = np.concatenate([t1, t2[1:]])

def fk(mu):
    def f(tt, y):
        r = np.sqrt(y[0]**2 + y[1]**2)
        return [y[2], y[3], -mu*y[0]/r**3, -mu*y[1]/r**3]
    return f
s1 = wie.solve(fk(mu_old), [a0, 0.0, 0.0, v0], t1*wie.day)
s2 = wie.solve(fk(mu_new), list(s1[-1]), (t2 - tc_d)*wie.day)
rel = np.vstack([s1, s2[1:]])
n1 = len(t1)
dist = np.hypot(rel[:, 0], rel[:, 1])
tf = np.linspace(0, P_new_d*wie.day, 20001)
sf = wie.solve(fk(mu_new), list(s1[-1]), tf)
rf = np.hypot(sf[:, 0], sf[:, 1])
r_peri_num = np.min(rf)
t_peri = tc_d + tf[np.argmin(rf)]/wie.day
E_end = 0.5*(s2[-1, 2]**2 + s2[-1, 3]**2) - mu_new/np.hypot(s2[-1, 0], s2[-1, 1])

before = np.arange(len(td)) < n1
Mp = np.where(before, wie.M_earth, M_gold)
Mt = Mp + wie.M_moon
relp = np.c_[rel[:, 0], rel[:, 1], 0*td]
planet = -relp*(wie.M_moon/Mt)[:, None]/R
moon = relp*(Mp/Mt)[:, None]/R
earth_pos = planet.copy(); earth_pos[~before] = np.nan
gold_pos = planet.copy(); gold_pos[before] = np.nan

# tidal stretch of the Moon: tidal/self gravity ratio drives a visual elongation
tid_ratio = 3*(Mp/wie.M_moon)*(wie.R_moon/dist)**3
stretch = 1 + 0.5*tid_ratio/np.max(tid_ratio)*0.3
moon_scale = np.c_[stretch, 1/np.sqrt(stretch), 1/np.sqrt(stretch)]

def tide(Mplanet, r):
    return 1.5*(wie.M_moon/Mplanet)*(R/r)**3*R
tide_today = tide(wie.M_earth, a0)
tide_t = tide(Mp, dist)
tide_peri = tide(M_gold, r_peri)
ang = np.degrees(2*wie.R_moon/dist)
ang_today = np.degrees(2*wie.R_moon/a0)
ang_peri = np.degrees(2*wie.R_moon/r_peri)
scale_kg = np.where(before, 70.0, weight70)
press = np.where(before, 1.013, p_bar)

s = wie.Scene(td, time_unit="days", length_unit="Earth radii")
spin = 2*np.pi*wie.day/86164.0
s.body("Earth", earth_pos, radius=1.0, kind="earth", spin=spin)
s.body("Gold Earth", gold_pos, radius=1.0, kind="planet", color="#d4af37", spin=spin)
s.body("Moon", moon, radius=wie.R_moon/R, kind="moon", spin=2*np.pi/P_real_d, scale=moon_scale)
s.curve("Moon path", moon, color="#bbbbbb", width=0.6)
th = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 120)
s.curve("Fluid Roche limit", np.c_[np.cos(th), np.sin(th), 0*th]*roche_fluid/R, color="#ff5555", width=0.5)
s.curve("Rigid Roche limit", np.c_[np.cos(th), np.sin(th), 0*th]*roche_rigid/R, color="#ffaa33", width=0.5)
s.change(td[n1], "Earth turns into solid gold, same size")

s.series("Earth-Moon distance", dist/1e3, "km")
s.series("Lunar tide range (equilibrium)", tide_t, "m")
s.on_earth("Bathroom scale reading for a 70 kg person", scale_kg, "kg", today=70.0)
s.on_earth("Air pressure at sea level (same air)", press, "bar", today=1.013)
s.on_earth("Lunar tide range (open ocean, equilibrium)", tide_t, "m", today=tide_today)
s.on_earth("Moon's size in the sky", ang, "degrees", today=ang_today)

s.number("Gold Earth mass", ratio, "× real Earth", f"Mean density {rho_mean:.0f} kg/m³ after self-compression")
s.number("Surface gravity", g_gold, "m/s²", f"Real Earth: {g_real:.2f} m/s²")
s.number("Weight of a 70 kg person", weight70, "kg on a scale", "Same body, stronger pull")
s.number("Central pressure", P_center_GPa, "GPa", f"Gold squeezed to {rho_c:.0f} kg/m³ at the centre")
s.number("Moon's closest approach", r_peri/1e3, "km", f"Today {a0/1e3:.0f} km; fluid Roche limit {roche_fluid/1e3:.0f} km, rigid limit {roche_rigid/1e3:.0f} km")
s.number("Moon's new orbital period", P_new_d, "days", f"Today {P_real_d:.2f} days")

s.caption(0, f"Today: rocky Earth, g = {g_real:.2f} m/s², Moon circling every {P_real_d:.2f} days at {a0/1e3:.0f} km")
s.caption(td[n1], f"Earth becomes gold: squeezed to {rho_c:.0f} kg/m³ at the centre, it is {ratio:.2f} times heavier")
s.caption(tc_d + 0.5, f"Gravity jumps to {g_gold:.1f} m/s²: a 70 kg person reads {weight70:.0f} kg; escape speed {v_esc:.1f} km/s")
s.caption(t_peri, f"Moon swoops to {r_peri/1e3:.0f} km, appears {ang_peri:.1f}° wide; tides reach {tide_peri:.1f} m")
s.caption(tc_d + 1.6*P_new_d, f"Orbit: eccentricity {e_new:.2f}, period {P_new_d:.1f} days. Perigee is {roche_txt}")

s.earth_event(td[n1], f"Everyone suddenly weighs {weight70/70:.1f} times more; standing up is exhausting")
s.earth_event(tc_d + 0.3, f"Air pressure jumps to about {p_bar:.1f} bar as the atmosphere is pulled down")
s.earth_event(t_peri, f"The Moon looms {ang_peri:.1f}° wide, tides of {tide_peri:.1f} m sweep the coasts")
s.earth_event(tc_d + P_new_d, f"A month now lasts only {P_new_d:.1f} days")

s.check("Baseline: real Earth surface gravity", g_real, 9.81, rtol=0.01)
s.check("Baseline: real Moon sidereal period (days)", P_real_d, 27.32, rtol=0.005)
s.check("Low-pressure limit matches uniform-sphere hydrostatics", R_small, R_small_exp, rtol=2e-3)
s.check("Mass equals integral of density profile", M_trap, M_gold, rtol=1e-4)
s.check("Orbit energy matches vis-viva -mu/2a", E_end, -mu_new/(2*a_new), rtol=1e-6)
s.check("Numerical perigee matches Kepler a(1-e)", r_peri_num, r_peri, rtol=1e-4)

if inside_rigid:
    fate = "close enough to be torn apart"
elif inside_fluid:
    fate = f"inside the {roche_fluid/1e3:.0f} km fluid Roche limit, so its solid rock would be heavily strained but probably hold"
else:
    fate = "still safely outside the Roche limit"
s.answer(f"A gold Earth would be {ratio:.2f} times heavier: gravity {g_gold:.1f} m/s², so a 70 kg person weighs like {weight70:.0f} kg. The Moon would plunge into a stretched orbit reaching {r_peri/1e3:.0f} km, {fate}.")

s.explain(f"We model gold under its own weight with hydrostatic equilibrium, dP/dr = -G m(r) rho / r^2 and dm/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho, plus the Murnaghan equation of state rho = rho0 (1 + K' P / K0)^(1/K'), with rho0 = {rho0:.0f} kg/m³, K0 = 167 GPa and K' = 6. Solving for a body of Earth's radius gives a central pressure of {P_center_GPa:.0f} GPa, central density {rho_c:.0f} kg/m³, mean density {rho_mean:.0f} kg/m³ and mass {ratio:.2f} Earth masses.\n\nNewton's law of universal gravitation, g = G M / R^2, gives {g_gold:.1f} m/s² instead of {g_real:.2f} m/s²; escape speed sqrt(2GM/R) rises from {v_esc_real:.1f} to {v_esc:.1f} km/s. Holding the same air, surface pressure scales with g to about {p_bar:.1f} bar.\n\nThe Moon keeps its {v0:.0f} m/s, now far below circular speed. The vis-viva equation v^2 = mu (2/r - 1/a) gives a semi-major axis of {a_new/1e3:.0f} km, eccentricity {e_new:.2f}, perigee {r_peri/1e3:.0f} km and period {P_new_d:.1f} days, confirmed numerically. The Roche limit d = k R (rho_planet/rho_moon)^(1/3) is {roche_fluid/1e3:.0f} km for a fluid Moon (k = 2.44) and {roche_rigid/1e3:.0f} km for a rigid one (k = 1.26); perigee is {roche_txt}.\n\nThe equilibrium lunar tide h = 1.5 (M_moon/M_planet)(R/r)^3 R rises from {tide_today:.2f} m to {tide_peri:.1f} m at perigee.")
s.camera(focus="Gold Earth", view="top")

assumptions: Earth keeps its radius and is replaced by pure gold.
The Murnaghan equation of state (K0 = 167 GPa, K' = 6) is extrapolated to roughly 10 TPa at the centre; this high-pressure behaviour is uncertain and the mass factor depends on it.
Temperature effects on gold's density and any melting of the interior are ignored.
The transformation is instantaneous; the Moon keeps its position and velocity at that moment.
The Moon is a point mass in its orbit; tidal breakup is judged only by the classical fluid and rigid Roche limits, and tidal dissipation is ignored.
The Moon's drawn stretching is illustrative, scaled by the computed tidal-to-self-gravity ratio.
Earth keeps its 23.93 hour rotation; the change in moment of inertia is ignored.
The atmosphere and oceans keep their mass; surface pressure scales with gravity.
Tides are equilibrium open-ocean tides from the Moon only; the Sun is ignored.

import numpy as np
import wie
from scipy.special import ellipk

G = wie.G
M = wie.M_earth
Re = wie.R_earth
rho = M / (4.0 / 3.0 * np.pi * Re**3)
R = np.pi * Re                      # pole-to-equator-to-"south" distance becomes the disk radius
h = (4.0 / 3.0 * Re**3) / R**2      # same volume

def ring_phi(a, m, r, z):
    s2 = (a + r)**2 + z**2
    k2 = 4.0 * a * r / s2
    return -2.0 * G * m * ellipk(k2) / (np.pi * np.sqrt(s2))

def field(src_a, src_z, src_m, r, z, d=500.0):
    A = src_a[None, :]; Z = src_z[None, :]; Mm = src_m[None, :]
    rr = np.asarray(r, float)[:, None]; zz = np.asarray(z, float)[:, None]
    def phi(rx, zx):
        return ring_phi(A, Mm, rx, zx - Z).sum(axis=1)
    ar = -(phi(rr + d, zz) - phi(np.abs(rr - d), zz)) / (2 * d)
    ar = np.where(np.asarray(r) < d, 0.0, ar)
    az = -(phi(rr, zz + d) - phi(rr, zz - d)) / (2 * d)
    return ar, az

# disk built from rings
NR, NL = 400, 20
dr, dz = R / NR, h / NL
a_i = (np.arange(NR) + 0.5) * dr
z_j = -h / 2 + (np.arange(NL) + 0.5) * dz
AA, ZZ = np.meshgrid(a_i, z_j)
src_a = AA.ravel(); src_z = ZZ.ravel()
src_m = rho * 2 * np.pi * src_a * dr * dz

r_s = np.linspace(0, R, 81)
ar_top, az_top = field(src_a, src_z, src_m, r_s, np.full_like(r_s, h / 2))
gmag = np.hypot(ar_top, az_top)
tilt = np.degrees(np.arctan2(np.abs(ar_top), np.abs(az_top)))
g_pole = gmag[0]
i_eq = np.argmin(np.abs(r_s - R / 2))
g_eq, tilt_eq = gmag[i_eq], tilt[i_eq]
g_rim, tilt_rim = gmag[-1], tilt[-1]

r_mid = np.linspace(0, R, 81)
ar_mid, _ = field(src_a, src_z, src_m, r_mid, np.zeros_like(r_mid))
P_c = rho * np.trapezoid(np.abs(ar_mid), r_mid)

phi_mid = ring_phi(src_a[None, :], src_m[None, :], a_i[:, None], 0.0 - src_z[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
m_ring = rho * 2 * np.pi * a_i * dr * h
U_disk = 0.5 * np.sum(m_ring * phi_mid)
U_sph = -0.6 * G * M**2 / Re
dU = U_disk - U_sph
cp = 1200.0
dT = dU / M / cp

# Baseline: same ring code applied to today's round Earth (uniform sphere)
nr2, nz2 = 150, 300
ra = (np.arange(nr2) + 0.5) * Re / nr2
za = -Re + (np.arange(nz2) + 0.5) * 2 * Re / nz2
RA, ZA = np.meshgrid(ra, za)
inside = RA**2 + ZA**2 <= Re**2
sa = RA[inside]; sz = ZA[inside]
sm = rho * 2 * np.pi * sa * (Re / nr2) * (2 * Re / nz2)
ar_s, _ = field(sa, sz, sm, np.array([2 * Re]), np.array([0.0]))
g_sphere_ring = 4 * abs(ar_s[0])
g_sph = G * M / Re**2

# analytic on-axis field of a uniform cylinder at the centre of its top face
g_pole_analytic = 2 * np.pi * G * rho * (h + R - np.sqrt(R**2 + h**2))

# collapse of the rim (radial free fall from rest)
a_rim = abs(ar_mid[-1])
mu = a_rim * R**2
sf = Re / R
x = sf
t_c = np.sqrt(R**3 / (2 * mu)) * (np.sqrt(x * (1 - x)) + np.arccos(np.sqrt(x)))
v_rim = np.sqrt(2 * mu / R * (1 / sf - 1))

T0 = 25 * 60.0
n_b, n_in = 50, 170
tb = np.linspace(0, T0, n_b, endpoint=False)
tin = np.linspace(0, t_c, n_in)
tpost = np.linspace(t_c, 1.3 * t_c, 51)[1:]
t = np.concatenate([tb, T0 + tin, T0 + tpost])
F = len(t)
before = np.arange(F) < n_b

sol = wie.solve(lambda tt, y: [y[1], -(a_rim / R) / y[0]**2], [1.0, 0.0], tin)
s_end = sol[-1, 0]
s_arr = np.full(F, sf)
s_arr[before] = 1.0
s_arr[n_b:n_b + n_in] = np.maximum(sol[:, 0], sf)
w = (1 - s_arr) / (1 - sf)
frac = np.clip((1 / s_arr - 1) / (1 / sf - 1), 0, 1)
Temp = 288.0 + dT * frac

# particles
N = 2400
k = np.arange(N)
pr = R * np.sqrt((k + 0.5) / N)
pphi = k * np.pi * (3 - np.sqrt(5))
pz = h * (((k * 0.618034) % 1.0) - 0.5)
disk = np.c_[pr * np.cos(pphi), pr * np.sin(pphi), pz]
th = np.pi * pr / R
rad = Re * (1 - 0.5 * (h / 2 - pz) / h)
sph = np.c_[rad * np.sin(th) * np.cos(pphi), rad * np.sin(th) * np.sin(pphi), rad * np.cos(th)]
pts = (1 - w)[:, None, None] * disk[None] + w[:, None, None] * sph[None]
pts[before] = 0.93 * sph[None]          # hidden inside the real Earth before the change
km = 1e-3
tm = t / 60.0
tchg = T0 / 60.0
sc = wie.Scene(tm, time_unit="min", length_unit="km")

epos = np.zeros((F, 3)); epos[~before] = np.nan
sc.body("Earth", epos, radius=Re * km, kind="earth", spin=2 * np.pi / (86164.0 / 60.0))
sc.cloud("Flat Earth rock", pts * km, color="#6b8f4e", size=1.5, temperature=Temp)
for j, rr in enumerate([0.0, 0.25 * R, 0.5 * R, 0.75 * R, 0.98 * R]):
    ii = np.argmin(np.abs(r_s - rr))
    gx, gz = ar_top[ii], az_top[ii]
    gn = np.hypot(gx, gz)
    p0 = np.array([r_s[ii], 0, h / 2])
    p1 = p0 + 2.5e6 * np.array([gx, 0, gz]) / gn
    seg = np.repeat(np.array([p0, p1])[None] * km, F, axis=0)
    seg[(w > 0.05) | before] = np.nan
    sc.curve(f"Gravity arrow {j+1}", seg, color="#ffcc33", width=2.0)
sc.change(tchg, "Earth is pressed into a flat disk with the same mass")

sc.series("Disk radius", np.where(before, Re, s_arr * R) / 1e3, "km")
sc.series("Mean temperature", Temp, "K")

sc.number("Gravity at the North Pole (disk centre)", g_pole, "m/s²", f"round Earth: {g_sph:.2f} m/s²")
sc.number("Gravity tilt at the equator ring", tilt_eq, "degrees", "how far 'down' leans toward the pole")
sc.number("Gravity tilt at the rim", tilt_rim, "degrees", "the edge feels like a steep uphill slope")
sc.number("Central crushing pressure", P_c / 1e9, "GPa", "rock fails at about 0.2 GPa")
sc.number("Collapse time to a ball", t_c / 60, "min", f"rim falls inward from {R/1e3:,.0f} km")
sc.number("Temperature rise from collapse", dT, "K", "gravitational energy turned to heat")

sc.caption(0, f"Today: a round Earth, radius {Re/1e3:,.0f} km, surface gravity {g_sph:.2f} m/s² everywhere, pointing straight down.")
sc.caption(tchg, f"Flattened: a disk {2*R/1e3:,.0f} km wide and {h/1e3:.0f} km thick. Gravity at the North Pole drops to {g_pole:.2f} m/s².")
sc.caption(tchg + 2, f"Gravity pulls toward the centre: at the equator ring 'down' tilts {tilt_eq:.0f}°, at the rim {tilt_rim:.0f}°. Midplane pressure {P_c/1e9:.0f} GPa crushes the rock.")
sc.caption(tchg + 0.5 * t_c / 60, "Rock cannot resist: the rim falls inward and the disk curls up into a ball.")
sc.caption(tchg + t_c / 60, f"After {t_c/60:.0f} min Earth is a sphere again; the rim hit at {v_rim/1e3:.1f} km/s and the rock heated by {dT:,.0f} K.")

kg_b = 70 * g_sph / wie.g0
scale = np.where(before, kg_b, (1 - w) * 70 * g_pole / wie.g0 + w * kg_b)
tempC = np.where(before, 15.0, Temp - 273.15)
tiltE = np.where(before, 0.0, (1 - w) * tilt_eq)
sc.on_earth("Bathroom scale at the North Pole (70 kg person)", scale, "kg", today=kg_b)
sc.on_earth("Average surface temperature", tempC, "°C", today=15.0)
sc.on_earth("Tilt of 'down' at the equator", tiltE, "degrees", today=0.0)

import numpy as np
import wie

G = wie.G; M = wie.M_earth; R = wie.R_earth
rho = M / (4.0 / 3.0 * np.pi * R**3)
L = (4.0 / 3.0 * np.pi) ** (1.0 / 3.0) * R   # same volume and mass as Earth
a = L / 2.0

def cube_field(P):
    P = np.atleast_2d(P)
    S = np.zeros(len(P)); gx = np.zeros(len(P)); gy = np.zeros(len(P)); gz = np.zeros(len(P))
    lim = [-a, a]
    for i in range(2):
        for j in range(2):
            for k in range(2):
                sg = (-1.0) ** (i + j + k + 1)
                x = lim[i] - P[:, 0]; y = lim[j] - P[:, 1]; z = lim[k] - P[:, 2]
                r = np.sqrt(x * x + y * y + z * z)
                lx = np.log(x + r); ly = np.log(y + r); lz = np.log(z + r)
                ax = np.arctan(y * z / (x * r)); ay = np.arctan(z * x / (y * r)); az = np.arctan(x * y / (z * r))
                S += sg * (x * y * lz + y * z * lx + z * x * ly - 0.5 * x * x * ax - 0.5 * y * y * ay - 0.5 * z * z * az)
                gx += sg * (y * lz + z * ly - x * ax)
                gy += sg * (z * lx + x * lz - y * ay)
                gz += sg * (x * ly + y * lx - z * az)
    return -G * rho * S, -G * rho * np.c_[gx, gy, gz]

h = 1.0
phi_c, g_c = cube_field(np.array([[0.0, 0.0, a + h]]))
phi_e, g_e = cube_field(np.array([[0.995 * a, 0.0, a + h]]))
phi_k, g_k = cube_field(np.array([[0.995 * a, 0.995 * a, a + h]]))
gc = np.linalg.norm(g_c[0]); ge = np.linalg.norm(g_e[0]); gk = np.linalg.norm(g_k[0])
tilt_e = np.degrees(np.arccos(-g_e[0, 2] / ge))
tilt_k = np.degrees(np.arccos(-g_k[0, 2] / gk))
g_sph = G * M / R**2

# Oceans settle on an equipotential around the face centres
n = 120
dx = L / n
uu = np.linspace(-a + dx / 2, a - dx / 2, n)
U, V = np.meshgrid(uu, uu)
phig, gg = cube_field(np.c_[U.ravel(), V.ravel(), np.full(n * n, a + h)])
gn = -gg[:, 2]
V_ocean = 1.335e18
def ocean_vol(ps):
    return 6 * np.sum(np.clip((ps - phig) / gn, 0, None)) * dx * dx
lo, hi = phig.min(), phig.max()
for it in range(80):
    mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    if ocean_vol(mid) > V_ocean:
        hi = mid
    else:
        lo = mid
phi_sea = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
depth = np.clip((phi_sea - phig) / gn, 0, None)
cover = np.mean(depth > 0) * 100
ocean_r_km = np.sqrt(np.sum(depth > 0) * dx * dx / np.pi) / 1e3
ocean_d_km = 2 * ocean_r_km
max_depth_km = depth.max() / 1e3
corner_h_km = (phi_k[0] - phi_sea) / gc / 1e3
p_corner = 100 * np.exp(-corner_h_km / 8.5)

# Self energy (Richardson extrapolated midpoint sums)
def U_cube(m):
    cc = np.linspace(-a + L / (2 * m), a - L / (2 * m), m)
    X, Y, Z = np.meshgrid(cc, cc, cc)
    ph, gt = cube_field(np.c_[X.ravel(), Y.ravel(), Z.ravel()])
    return 0.5 * rho * np.sum(ph) * (L / m) ** 3
Uc = (4 * U_cube(32) - U_cube(16)) / 3
Us = -0.6 * G * M**2 / R
E_rel = Uc - Us
dT = E_rel / (M * 1000.0)
E_mt = E_rel / 4.184e15

# Collapse: corners fall from sqrt(3) a to R (lower bound: free fall)
r0 = np.sqrt(3) * a
def t_of_r(r):
    x = r / r0
    return np.sqrt(r0**3 / (2 * G * M)) * (np.sqrt(x * (1 - x)) + np.arccos(np.sqrt(x)))
t_c = t_of_r(R); tc_min = t_c / 60
tt_num = np.linspace(0, t_c, 400)
sol = wie.solve(lambda tt, y: [y[1], -G * M / y[0]**2], [r0, 0.0], tt_num)

t0 = 10.0
tm = np.concatenate([np.linspace(0, t0, 50, endpoint=False), np.linspace(t0, t0 + 3 * tc_min, 200)])
F = len(tm)
rr = np.linspace(R, r0, 600); trr = t_of_r(rr) / 60
rc = np.interp(tm - t0, trr[::-1], rr[::-1])
f = np.clip((r0 - rc) / (r0 - R), 0, 1)
f = np.where(tm - t0 >= tc_min, 1.0, f)
before = tm < t0
cube_on = (tm >= t0) & (tm - t0 < tc_min)

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
pts = []
for axis in range(3):
    for sg in (-1, 1):
        p = rng.uniform(-a, a, (400, 3)); p[:, axis] = sg * a
        pts.append(p)
pts = np.vstack(pts)
sph = 0.99 * R * pts / np.linalg.norm(pts, axis=1)[:, None]
rock = (pts[None] + f[:, None, None] * (sph - pts)[None]) / 1e3
rock[before] = sph[None] / 1e3
Tcloud = np.where(before, 288.0, 288.0 + dT * f)

mask = depth > 0
oc_u = U.ravel()[mask]; oc_v = V.ravel()[mask]
sel = rng.choice(len(oc_u), size=min(120, len(oc_u)), replace=False)
oce = []
for axis in range(3):
    for sg in (-1, 1):
        p = np.zeros((len(sel), 3)); others = [q for q in range(3) if q != axis]
        p[:, axis] = sg * (a + 30e3); p[:, others[0]] = oc_u[sel]; p[:, others[1]] = oc_v[sel]
        oce.append(p)
oce = np.vstack(oce)
osph = 0.99 * R * oce / np.linalg.norm(oce, axis=1)[:, None]
ocean = (oce[None] + f[:, None, None] * (osph - oce)[None]) / 1e3
ocean[before] = osph[None] / 1e3

earth_pos = np.zeros((F, 3)); earth_pos[~before] = np.nan
molten = np.full((F, 3), np.nan); molten[(tm - t0) >= tc_min] = 0.0
spin = 2 * np.pi * 60 / 86164.0

s = wie.Scene(tm, time_unit="min", length_unit="km")
s.body("Earth", earth_pos, radius=R / 1e3, kind="earth", spin=spin)
s.cloud("Cube Earth rock", rock, color="#8a7a5a", size=1.5, temperature=Tcloud)
s.cloud("Face-centre seas", ocean, color="#2a6fdb", size=1.5)
s.body("Molten Earth", molten, radius=R / 1e3, kind="planet", color="#aa5533", temperature=288.0 + dT, spin=spin)

corner_series = np.where(before, R, rc) / 1e3
s.series("Corner distance from centre", corner_series, "km")
s.series("Average temperature", Tcloud - 273.15, "°C")

s.number("Cube side length", L / 1e3, "km", "same volume and mass as Earth")
s.number("Gravity at face centre", gc, "m/s²", f"round Earth: {g_sph:.2f} m/s²")
s.number("Gravity tilt near an edge", tilt_e, "degrees", "ground there feels like a steep hillside")
s.number("Diameter of each face-centre sea", ocean_d_km, "km", f"6 seas, max depth {max_depth_km:.1f} km")
s.number("Corner height above sea level", corner_h_km, "km", "equivalent height from gravitational potential")
s.number("Collapse time of the corners (lower bound)", tc_min, "min", "free fall; rock friction makes it longer")
s.number("Heating from collapse", dT, "K", "released energy spread through the whole planet")

s.caption(0, f"Today: round Earth, gravity {g_sph:.2f} m/s² everywhere, spinning once every 23.93 hours")
s.caption(t0, f"Cube Earth, {L/1e3:.0f} km on a side: {gc:.2f} m/s² at face centres, gravity tilted {tilt_e:.0f}° near edges")
s.caption(t0 + 0.1 * tc_min, f"Oceans pool into 6 round seas about {ocean_d_km:.0f} km across, up to {max_depth_km:.1f} km deep, covering {cover:.0f}% of the surface")
s.caption(t0 + 0.3 * tc_min, f"Corners sit {corner_h_km:.0f} km 'uphill' above sea level, far above the air; no rock can hold that up")
s.caption(t0 + tc_min, f"After at least {tc_min:.1f} min the corners have crashed down; {E_rel:.2e} J released heats the planet by {dT:.0f} K")

s.change(t0, "Earth becomes a cube of the same mass and volume")
s.earth_event(t0, f"A 70 kg person at a face centre weighs {70*gc/g_sph:.0f} kg on a scale")
s.earth_event(t0 + 0.1 * tc_min, f"Near the edges, flat ground feels like a {tilt_e:.0f}° slope; water rushes to the face centres")
s.earth_event(t0 + 0.3 * tc_min, f"Air at the corners: {p_corner:.1g}% of normal pressure, essentially space")
s.earth_event(t0 + tc_min, f"Corners collapse in at least {tc_min:.1f} min; the whole planet heats by {dT:.0f} K and melts")

scale_kg = np.where(cube_on, 70 * gc / g_sph, 70.0)
s.on_earth("Bathroom scale at a face centre (70 kg person)", scale_kg, "kg", today=70.0)
s.on_earth("Average surface temperature", Tcloud - 273.15, "°C", today=15.0)
s.on_earth("Air pressure at a corner", np.where(cube_on, p_corner * (1 - f), 100.0), "% of today", today=100.0)

pf, gf = cube_field(np.array([[20 * a, 0.0, 0.0]]))
s.check("Baseline: cube gravity far away equals Newton point mass", np.linalg.norm(gf[0]), G * M / (20 * a)**2, rtol=1e-4)
s.check("Baseline: round Earth surface gravity matches measured ~9.82 m/s²", g_sph, 9.82, rtol=0.01)
d = 100.0
pp, gt1 = cube_field(np.array([[0.0, 0.0, a + h + d]]))
pm, gt2 = cube_field(np.array([[0.0, 0.0, a + h - d]]))
s.check("field equals minus gradient of potential at face centre", -(pp[0] - pm[0]) / (2 * d), g_c[0, 2], rtol=1e-4)
s.check("cube self-energy matches published coefficient 0.94116 G M²/L", -Uc * L / (G * M**2), 0.9411563, rtol=3e-3)
s.check("analytic corner free-fall time matches numerical integration", sol[-1, 0], R, rtol=1e-6)
s.check("ocean volume conserved in the six seas", ocean_vol(phi_sea), V_ocean, rtol=1e-3)

s.answer(f"A cube Earth {L/1e3:.0f} km on a side could not last: its corners would crash down in at least {tc_min:.1f} min, heating the planet by {dT:.0f} K. Before that, oceans gather in 6 round seas about {ocean_d_km:.0f} km across and gravity tilts {tilt_e:.0f}° near the edges.")
s.explain(f"The cube has Earth's mass and volume, so its side is L = (4 pi / 3)^(1/3) R = {L/1e3:.0f} km. Its gravity comes from Newton's law of universal gravitation integrated exactly over a uniform-density cube (the closed-form prism potential). At a face centre g = {gc:.2f} m/s² versus {g_sph:.2f} m/s² for the sphere; near an edge the field is tilted {tilt_e:.0f}° from vertical and near a corner {tilt_k:.0f}°.\n\nWater follows equipotential surfaces. Solving for the level that holds 1.335e18 m³ of ocean gives six circular seas about {ocean_d_km:.0f} km in diameter and up to {max_depth_km:.1f} km deep, covering {cover:.0f}% of the surface. The corners sit about {corner_h_km:.0f} km 'uphill' in potential, far beyond the 8.5 km scale height of air, so they are airless.\n\nRock cannot support such slopes: the stress rho g h at the corners exceeds rock strength by orders of magnitude, so the planet relaxes to hydrostatic equilibrium (a sphere). Corners in free fall from {r0/1e3:.0f} km to {R/1e3:.0f} km take {tc_min:.1f} min, a lower bound since rock below resists.\n\nThe gravitational self-energy of a cube is -0.9412 G M²/L, compared with -0.6 G M²/R for a sphere. The difference, {E_rel:.2e} J (about {E_mt:.1e} megatons of TNT), heats rock with specific heat 1000 J/kg/K by {dT:.0f} K, melting the planet.")
s.camera(focus="Cube Earth rock", view="free")

assumptions: The cube has Earth's mass and volume, with uniform density.
Earth's spin is ignored in the cube's gravity field.

Corner height is an equivalent height from potential divided by face-centre gravity.
The collapse is modelled as corner free fall onto a point mass, so its time is a lower bound.
All released energy becomes heat, spread evenly with specific heat 1000 J/kg/K.
Guesswork starts here: how a cube Earth could form at all is not physics we can model; only its gravity and energy are computed.

from scipy.integrate import quad

G = wie.G; Me = wie.M_earth; Re = wie.R_earth; Ms = wie.M_sun; AU = wie.AU
Mv = 4.8675e24; Rv = 6.0518e6
mu_s = G * Ms

    return np.sqrt(mu_s / a)

def vesc(m, r):
    return np.sqrt(2 * G * m / r)

# Venus nudged onto an orbit with perihelion at Venus and aphelion at Earth
aE = AU; aV = 0.723332 * AU
vE = circ(aE)
at = (aE + aV) / 2
v_ap = np.sqrt(mu_s * (2 / aE - 1 / at))
vinf = vE - v_ap

M = Me + Mv; Rc = Re + Rv
mred = Me * Mv / M
v_mut = vesc(M, Rc)
v_imp_an = np.sqrt(v_mut**2 + vinf**2)

# Head-on approach from 40 Earth radii under mutual gravity
r0 = 40 * Re
vr0 = -np.sqrt(vinf**2 + 2 * G * M / r0)
t_c = quad(lambda r: 1.0 / np.sqrt(vinf**2 + 2 * G * M / r), Rc, r0, epsrel=1e-12)[0]
t_app = np.linspace(0, t_c, 80)
sol = wie.solve(lambda t, y: [y[1], -G * M / y[0]**2], [r0, vr0], t_app)
r = sol[:, 0]; vr = sol[:, 1]
v_imp = -vr[-1]
Espec = 0.5 * vr**2 - G * M / r

# Energy budget (uniform-density spheres)
def U(m, R):
    return 0.6 * G * m**2 / R
Rm = (Re**3 + Rv**3) ** (1 / 3)
E_rel = U(M, Rm) - U(Me, Re) - U(Mv, Rv) + 0.5 * mred * vinf**2
q = E_rel / M
melt_need = 1000.0 * 1500 + 4.0e5
melt_ratio = q / melt_need
g_m = G * M / Rm**2 / wie.g0
v_esc_m = vesc(M, Rm)
Tsurf = 2300.0
P_rad = 4 * np.pi * Rm**2 * wie.sigma_SB * Tsurf**4
t_cool_yr = E_rel / P_rad / wie.year
E_chx = 4.2e23
chx_ratio = E_rel / E_chx

# Ejecta: ballistic splash around the merged body
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
N = 2200
phi = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, N)
d = np.c_[rng.normal(0, 0.25, N), np.cos(phi), np.sin(phi)]
d /= np.linalg.norm(d, axis=1)[:, None]
tang = np.cross(d, np.array([1.0, 0, 0]))
tang /= np.linalg.norm(tang, axis=1)[:, None]

ang = rng.uniform(0.3, 1.0, N)

vel = (d * np.sin(ang)[:, None] + tang * np.cos(ang)[:, None]) * (u * v_esc_m)[:, None]

aloft = np.zeros(F2)

    ns = int(np.ceil(dt / 10.0)); h = dt / ns

        rr = np.linalg.norm(p, axis=1)[:, None]
        v = v - 0.5 * h * G * M * p / rr**3
        p = p + h * v
        rr = np.linalg.norm(p, axis=1)[:, None]
        v = v - 0.5 * h * G * M * p / rr**3

cloud = np.r_[np.full((F0 + F1, N, 3), np.nan), cloud_post]

s = wie.Scene(th, time_unit="hours", length_unit="Earth radii")
s.body("Earth", xE, radius=1.0, kind="earth", spin=2 * np.pi / 23.934)
s.body("Venus", xV, radius=Rv / Re, kind="planet", color="#e8c27a")
s.body("Merged magma planet", xM, radius=Rm / Re, kind="planet", color="#ff6a2a", temperature=Tsurf, scale=scale_m)
s.cloud("Molten debris", cloud, color="#ffae5a", size=0.8, temperature=3000.0)

speed = np.r_[np.full(F0, np.nan), -vr / 1e3, np.full(F2, np.nan)]
sep = np.r_[np.full(F0, np.nan), r / Re, np.full(F2, np.nan)]
s.series("Closing speed", speed, "km/s")
s.series("Centre separation", sep, "Earth radii")
s.series("Debris still aloft", np.r_[np.zeros(F0 + F1), aloft], "%")

s.number("Impact speed", v_imp / 1e3, "km/s", "mutual escape speed plus orbital mismatch")
s.number("Energy released", E_rel, "J", "kinetic plus gravitational settling")
s.number("Energy vs dinosaur-killing impact", chx_ratio, "times", "Chicxulub about 4.2e23 J")
s.number("Energy vs needed to melt both planets", melt_ratio, "times", "heat to 1500 K above today plus latent heat")
s.number("Surface gravity of merged planet", g_m, "g", f"mass {M/Me:.2f} Earth masses, radius {Rm/Re:.2f} Earth radii")

import numpy as np
import wie

G = wie.G; AU = wie.AU; yr = wie.year
M_star = 0.0898 * wie.M_sun
R_star = 0.1192 * wie.R_sun
T_star = 2566.0
MV_trappist = 18.80 - 5 * np.log10(12.47 / 10.0)
L_trappist_meas = 5.53e-4
mass_factor = M_star / wie.M_jupiter

def luminosity(R, T):
    return 4 * np.pi * R**2 * wie.sigma_SB * T**4

L_J = luminosity(R_star, T_star)
L_rel = L_J / wie.L_sun
L_pct = 100 * L_rel
MV_star = MV_trappist - 2.5 * np.log10(L_rel / L_trappist_meas)

aJ = 5.203 * AU
mS, mE = wie.M_sun, wie.M_earth
m1 = np.array([mS, mE, wie.M_jupiter])
m2 = np.array([mS, mE, M_star])

def period_yr(a, M):
    return 2 * np.pi * np.sqrt(a**3 / (G * M)) / yr
P_J_today = period_yr(aJ, mS + wie.M_jupiter)

eE0 = 0.0167
rpE = AU * (1 - eE0)
vE = np.sqrt(G * (mS + mE) * (1 + eE0) / rpE)
vJ = np.sqrt(G * (mS + wie.M_jupiter) / aJ)
pos0 = np.array([[0, 0, 0], [rpE, 0, 0], [0, aJ, 0]], float)
vel0 = np.array([[0, 0, 0], [0, vE, 0], [-vJ, 0, 0]], float)
pos0 -= (m1[:, None] * pos0).sum(0) / m1.sum()
vel0 -= (m1[:, None] * vel0).sum(0) / m1.sum()

def make_f(m):
    def f(t, y):
        p = y[:9].reshape(3, 3)
        d = p[None, :, :] - p[:, None, :]
        r2 = np.sum(d**2, -1) + np.eye(3)
        inv = (1 - np.eye(3)) / r2**1.5
        a = G * np.sum((m[None, :] * inv)[:, :, None] * d, axis=1)
        return np.concatenate([y[9:], a.ravel()])
    return f

def energy(y, m):
    p = y[:9].reshape(3, 3); v = y[9:].reshape(3, 3)
    K = 0.5 * np.sum(m * np.sum(v**2, 1))
    U = 0.0
    for i in range(3):
        for j in range(i + 1, 3):
            U -= G * m[i] * m[j] / np.linalg.norm(p[i] - p[j])
    return K + U

t_c = 6.0
T_end = 36.0
tb = np.linspace(0, t_c, 70)
ta = np.linspace(t_c, T_end, 231)
s1 = wie.solve(make_f(m1), np.concatenate([pos0.ravel(), vel0.ravel()]), tb * yr)
s2 = wie.solve(make_f(m2), s1[-1], ta * yr)

ty = np.concatenate([tb, ta[1:]])

after = ty > t_c
P = sol[:, :9].reshape(-1, 3, 3)
V = sol[:, 9:].reshape(-1, 3, 3)

# display in the centre-of-mass frame of each phase (removes the drift caused by the new mass)
mass_frames = np.where(after[:, None], m2[None, :], m1[None, :])
com = np.sum(mass_frames[:, :, None] * P, 1) / mass_frames.sum(1)[:, None]
Pd = (P - com[:, None, :]) / AU

# Jupiter's new orbit: analytic from the state at ignition
yc = s1[-1]
rv = yc[6:9] - yc[0:3]; vv = yc[15:18] - yc[9:12]
mu_f = G * (mS + M_star)
r0 = np.linalg.norm(rv); v0 = np.linalg.norm(vv)
hvec = np.cross(rv, vv)
evec0 = np.cross(vv, hvec) / mu_f - rv / r0
e_pred = np.linalg.norm(evec0)
a_new = 1 / (2 / r0 - v0**2 / mu_f)
P_new = 2 * np.pi * np.sqrt(a_new**3 / mu_f) / yr
rel = P[after, 2] - P[after, 0]; vrel = V[after, 2] - V[after, 0]
rr = np.linalg.norm(rel, axis=1)
hh = np.cross(rel, vrel)
ev = np.cross(vrel, hh) / mu_f - rel / rr[:, None]
e_sim = np.linalg.norm(ev, axis=1).mean()
E_start = energy(s2[0], m2); E_end = energy(s2[-1], m2)

# Earth's orbit eccentricity
relE = P[:, 1] - P[:, 0]; vrelE = V[:, 1] - V[:, 0]
dS = np.linalg.norm(relE, axis=1)
muE = G * (mS + mE)
hE = np.cross(relE, vrelE)
eE = np.linalg.norm(np.cross(vrelE, hE) / muE - relE / dS[:, None], axis=1)
e_swing = eE[after].max() - eE[after].min()

# Light at Earth
dJ = np.linalg.norm(P[:, 1] - P[:, 2], axis=1)
dJS = np.linalg.norm(P[:, 2] - P[:, 0], axis=1)

F1 = wie.L_sun / (4 * np.pi * AU**2)
flux_ppm_max = 1e6 * F_J.max() / F1

dT = T_surf - 288.15
dT_mK = 1000 * dT.max()

pc_au = wie.pc / AU
m_star_app = MV_star + 5 * np.log10(dJ / AU / pc_au / 10.0)
m_planet = -9.40 + 5 * np.log10((dJS / AU) * (dJ / AU))

m_best = m_star_app[after].min()
m_faint = m_star_app[after].max()
m_planet_best = m_planet[~after].min()
venus_brighter = 10 ** (-0.4 * (m_best - (-4.6)))
moon_fainter = 10 ** (-0.4 * (-12.74 - m_best))
moon_pct = 100 * 10 ** (-0.4 * (m_app + 12.74))
venus_ratio = 10 ** (-0.4 * (m_app + 4.6))
wobble_au = (aJ * M_star / (mS + M_star)) / AU
hill_au = aJ * (M_star / (3 * (mS + M_star))) ** (1 / 3) / AU
lam_peak_um = 2.897771955e-3 / T_star * 1e6
i_best = np.argmin(np.where(after, m_app, 99))

s = wie.Scene(ty, time_unit="yr", length_unit="AU")
nanb = np.full((F, 3), np.nan)
jp = Pd[:, 2].copy(); jp[after] = np.nan
js = Pd[:, 2].copy(); js[~after] = np.nan
s.body("Sun", Pd[:, 0], radius=0.25, kind="star", temperature=5772.0)
s.body("Jupiter", jp, radius=0.12, kind="planet")
s.body("Star Jupiter", js, radius=0.15, kind="star", color="#ff5522", temperature=T_star)
s.body("Earth", Pd[:, 1], radius=0.08, kind="earth")
s.curve("Earth's path", Pd[:, 1], color="#66aaff", width=1.0)
s.curve("Jupiter's path", Pd[:, 2], color="#ff8844", width=1.0)
s.curve("Sun's wobble", Pd[:, 0], color="#ffee88", width=1.0)

s.series("Jupiter's magnitude in Earth's sky (lower = brighter)", m_app, "mag")
s.series("Earth orbital eccentricity", eE, "")
s.series("Extra warming of Earth", dT * 1000, "mK")

s.number("Mass Jupiter must gain", mass_factor, "× Jupiter's mass", "To reach 0.0898 solar masses, like the real red dwarf TRAPPIST-1")
s.number("Star Jupiter luminosity", L_pct, "% of Sun", f"A 2566 K red dwarf, peak emission at {lam_peak_um:.2f} µm (infrared)")
s.number("Brightest magnitude from Earth", m_best, "mag", f"Today Jupiter peaks near {m_planet_best:.1f}")
s.number("Brighter than Venus", venus_brighter, "times", "At its closest")
s.number("Fainter than the full Moon", moon_fainter, "times", "At its closest")
s.number("Maximum warming of Earth", dT_mK, "mK", "Thousandths of a degree")
s.caption(0, f"Today: Jupiter is a planet orbiting every {P_J_today:.2f} yr, shining by reflected light at magnitude {m_planet_best:.1f} at best")
s.change(t_c, "Jupiter gains mass and ignites as a red dwarf star")
s.caption(t_c, f"Jupiter gains {mass_factor:.0f} times its mass and ignites at 2566 K, glowing at {L_pct:.3f}% of the Sun's power")
s.caption(t_c + 2, f"Its orbit turns eccentric (e = {e_pred:.3f}), now {P_new:.2f} yr long; the Sun swings {wobble_au:.2f} AU around the shared centre of mass")
s.caption(ty[i_best], f"Closest pass: magnitude {m_best:.1f}, {venus_brighter:.0f} times brighter than Venus but {moon_fainter:.0f} times fainter than the full Moon")
s.caption(T_end - 6, f"Earth's warming peaks at just {dT_mK:.1f} mK; its orbit's eccentricity swings by {e_swing:.4f}")

s.on_earth("Average surface temperature", T_surf - 273.15, "°C", today=15.0)
s.on_earth("Jupiter's light vs the full Moon", moon_pct, "%")
s.on_earth("Jupiter's brightness vs Venus", venus_ratio, "×")
s.earth_event(0, f"Jupiter is a bright dot at magnitude {m_planet_best:.1f} in the night sky")
s.earth_event(t_c, "Jupiter flares into a reddish-orange star visible even in daylight")
s.earth_event(ty[i_best], f"At closest, Star Jupiter casts faint shadows: {moon_fainter:.0f}× dimmer than a full Moon")
s.earth_event(T_end - 4, f"Climate barely notices: at most {dT_mK:.1f} mK of warming")

s.check("Baseline: Jupiter's orbital period today (Kepler's third law) vs measured 11.862 yr", P_J_today, 11.862, rtol=0.01)
s.check("Baseline: Stefan-Boltzmann luminosity of TRAPPIST-1 vs measured 5.53e-4 L_sun", L_rel, L_trappist_meas, rtol=0.05)
s.check("Simulated Jupiter eccentricity matches two-body prediction after ignition", e_sim, e_pred, rtol=0.05)
s.check("Energy conserved after ignition", E_end, E_start, rtol=1e-6)

s.explain(f"Hydrogen fusion needs a core hot and dense enough, which requires at least about 0.075 solar masses. We model Star Jupiter on the measured red dwarf TRAPPIST-1: 0.0898 solar masses, which is {mass_factor:.0f} times Jupiter's mass, with a radius of 0.1192 solar radii and a temperature of 2566 K. The Stefan-Boltzmann law, L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4, gives {L_pct:.3f}% of the Sun's luminosity, mostly infrared (Wien peak {lam_peak_um:.2f} µm).\n\nGravity follows Newton's law of universal gravitation in a three-body integration (Sun, Earth, Jupiter). The added mass moves with Jupiter, so the stronger pull bends Jupiter onto an eccentric orbit with e = {e_pred:.3f} and period {P_new:.2f} yr. The Sun now circles the barycentre at {wobble_au:.2f} AU, and Star Jupiter's Hill sphere spans {hill_au:.2f} AU, reaching toward the outer asteroid belt. Earth's eccentricity varies by {e_swing:.4f} over the run.\n\nThe inverse-square law gives at most {flux_ppm_max:.1f} parts per million of sunlight at Earth. Radiative balance, T proportional to flux^(1/4), turns that into {dT_mK:.1f} mK of warming. GMs = wie.G * wie.M_sun

data = [("Mercury",1.660e-7,0.387,"#a0a0a0",100),("Venus",2.448e-6,0.723,"#e8c27a",200),
        ("Earth",3.003e-6,1.0,"#4a8cff",105),("Mars",3.227e-7,1.524,"#d0603a",160),
        ("Jupiter",9.546e-4,5.203,"#d8b48a",95),("Saturn",2.858e-4,9.537,"#e8d8a0",355),
        ("Uranus",4.366e-5,19.19,"#9fe0e8",55),("Neptune",5.151e-5,30.07,"#4060e0",0)]
t_ch = 1.0
t_yr = np.concatenate([np.linspace(0, t_ch, 50), np.linspace(t_ch + 0.01, t_ch + 11.86, 200)])
after = t_yr >= t_ch
t_s = t_yr * wie.year
pos = {}; periods = {}
for name, m, a, col, L0 in data:
    P = 2*np.pi*np.sqrt((a*wie.AU)**3/GMs)
    periods[name] = P
    ang_before = np.radians(L0) + 2*np.pi*t_s/P
    ang_after = 2*np.pi*(t_s - t_ch*wie.year)/P
    ang = np.where(after, ang_after, ang_before)
    pos[name] = np.c_[a*np.cos(ang), a*np.sin(ang), 0*ang]

R = wie.R_earth
tid_tot = np.zeros_like(t_yr); h_tot = np.zeros_like(t_yr)
tid_al = {}
ich = np.argmax(after)
for name, m, a, col, L0 in data:
    if name == "Earth":
        continue
    d = np.linalg.norm(pos[name]-pos["Earth"], axis=1)*wie.AU
    M = m*wie.M_sun
    tid = 2*wie.G*M*R/d**3
    tid_al[name] = tid[ich]
    tid_tot += tid
    h_tot += (M/wie.M_earth)*R**4/d**3
tid_moon = 2*wie.G*wie.M_moon*R/wie.a_moon**3
h_moon = (wie.M_moon/wie.M_earth)*R**4/wie.a_moon**3
tid_sun = 2*GMs*R/wie.AU**3
ratio_today = tid_tot[0]/tid_moon*1e6
ratio_al = tid_tot[ich]/tid_moon*1e6
h_al_mm = h_tot[ich]*1e3
h_today_mm = h_tot[0]*1e3
weight_ng = 70.0*tid_tot/wie.g0*1e12   # nanograms on a 70 kg person's scale
w_al_ng = weight_ng[ich]

angs = np.array([np.degrees(np.arctan2(pos[n][:,1], pos[n][:,0])) % 360 for n,_,_,_,_ in data])
spread = np.zeros(len(t_yr))
for i in range(len(t_yr)):
    s_ = np.sort(angs[:, i]); gaps = np.diff(np.r_[s_, s_[0]+360])
    spread[i] = 360 - gaps.max()
i1 = np.argmin(np.abs(t_yr-(t_ch+1.0)))
sp1 = spread[i1]
venus_ppm = tid_al["Venus"]/tid_moon*1e6
jup_ppm = tid_al["Jupiter"]/tid_moon*1e6
merc_days = periods["Mercury"]/wie.day
jup_yr = periods["Jupiter"]/wie.year

s = wie.Scene(t_yr, time_unit="yr", length_unit="AU")

vis = {"Mercury":0.05,"Venus":0.09,"Earth":0.1,"Mars":0.07,"Jupiter":0.5,"Saturn":0.45,"Uranus":0.32,"Neptune":0.32}
th = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 160)
for name, m, a, col, L0 in data:
    s.body(name, pos[name], radius=vis[name], kind="earth" if name=="Earth" else "planet", color=col)
    s.curve(name+" orbit", np.c_[a*np.cos(th), a*np.sin(th), 0*th], color="#334455", width=0.5)
s.curve("Line-up", np.array([[0,0,0],[31,0,0]]), color="#ffdd55", width=1.0)

s.series("Planets' tidal pull on Earth / Moon's", tid_tot/tid_moon*1e6, "ppm")
s.series("Spread of the planets around the Sun", spread, "deg")
s.series("Extra tide from planets", h_tot*1e3, "mm")

s.number("Planets' combined tidal pull on Earth, lined up", ratio_al, "ppm of the Moon's", "millionths of the Moon's tidal effect")
s.number("Planets' combined tidal pull on Earth, today's layout", ratio_today, "ppm of the Moon's", "for comparison")
s.number("Extra ocean tide from the line-up", h_al_mm, "mm", "equilibrium tide height")

s.caption(0, f"Today: the planets are scattered around the Sun. Together their tides on Earth are {ratio_today:.0f} ppm of the Moon's")
s.change(t_ch, "All eight planets line up on one side of the Sun")
s.caption(t_ch + 0.05, f"Lined up, their combined tidal stretch on Earth is {ratio_al:.0f} ppm of the Moon's, which raises the oceans by {h_al_mm:.3f} mm")
s.caption(t_ch + 0.5, f"Venus does most of it ({venus_ppm:.0f} ppm of the Moon's). Jupiter is huge but far away ({jup_ppm:.0f} ppm), because tides weaken as 1/distance cubed")

s.caption(t_ch + 6.0, f"The Moon's tide is about {h_moon:.2f} m, so the planets add next to nothing")
s.caption(t_ch + 11.8, f"One Jupiter year later ({jup_yr:.2f} yr), nothing on Earth has noticed")

s.on_earth("Extra ocean tide from the planets", h_tot*1e3, "mm")
s.on_earth("Change in a 70 kg person's scale reading", weight_ng, "ng")
s.on_earth("Planets' tidal pull vs the Moon's", tid_tot/tid_moon*1e6, "ppm")
s.earth_event(0.1, f"A normal day: the Moon's tides rise and fall about {h_moon:.2f} m")
